title: The Witcher 3: A Monster Hunter with a Heart
ru: Почему The Witcher 3 до сих пор называют одной из лучших RPG
text:
Imagine a side quest about a missing wife that slowly turns into one of the darkest, saddest stories you have ever seen in a video game. That, in a nutshell, is The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — and it's one of the reasons why players still talk about it more than ten years after its release.

The game came out in 2015. It was made by CD Projekt Red, a studio from Poland, and it is based on the fantasy books by the Polish writer Andrzej Sapkowski. That same year, it won Game of the Year at The Game Awards, beating some very strong competition.

You play as Geralt of Rivia, a witcher — a professional monster hunter. Witchers are trained from childhood and changed by dangerous potions, so they are faster and stronger than ordinary people. Villagers need them when a monster appears, but they don't like them or trust them. Geralt doesn't talk much, but he has a dry sense of humour and his own rules about right and wrong.

In the main story, Geralt is searching for Ciri, a young woman he raised almost like a daughter. The Wild Hunt, a band of ghostly riders from another world, is chasing her too. The search takes him through villages ruined by war, rich and noisy cities, and cold islands in the far north.

So what makes the game special? First, the quests. Even a small job, like clearing a monster's nest for a few coins, can become a funny, sad or strange story with a twist at the end. Second, your choices matter, but not in an obvious way. Sometimes a decision seems kind, and you only see its consequences hours later. Plenty of players have paused the game just to sit and think about what they had done.

Then there's Gwent, a card game that people play in the taverns of the game world. It was meant to be a small extra, but players loved it so much that it was later released as a separate game.

Add two excellent expansions, Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine, and you get a game that can easily take a hundred hours. Somehow, almost every one of them feels worth it.

title: Skyrim: The Game That Never Gets Old
ru: Skyrim: свобода, драконы и моды, благодаря которым в игру играют больше десяти лет
text:
“Hey, you. You're finally awake.” If you have spent any time online, you have probably seen this line. It comes from the opening of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, where your character wakes up on a cart full of prisoners who are on their way to be executed. Not a great start to the day. Luckily, a dragon interrupts.

Skyrim was released by the American studio Bethesda Game Studios on 11 November 2011 — or 11.11.11, a date fans loved. The game is set in Skyrim, a cold northern land of snowy mountains, pine forests and ancient tombs full of the restless dead. Dragons, which everyone thought were only legends, have suddenly returned. Your hero turns out to be the Dragonborn, a person with the soul of a dragon, who can learn the dragons' language and use its words as magical shouts. Shout the right words at an enemy, and they might fly right off a mountain.

But the main quest is only a small part of the game. Skyrim is really about freedom. You can be a warrior with a huge axe, a sneaky thief, a mage, or a bit of everything. You can join a guild of thieves, buy a house, get married, or simply walk towards a mountain on the horizon — and then actually climb it. Many people have played for hundreds of hours without finishing the main story.

The guards of Skyrim have become famous too. Many of them tell you that they were once adventurers too — until they took an arrow in the knee. For some reason, this sad little story turned into one of the biggest internet jokes of its year.

Another secret of Skyrim's long life is mods — changes and additions made by fans. Some mods make the game look modern, others add whole new cities and stories, and some simply replace the dragons with a smiling cartoon train. Bethesda, meanwhile, has re-released the game on so many devices that this has become a joke as well.

Yes, Skyrim has bugs. Horses climb almost vertical cliffs, and giants can send you flying high into the sky with one hit. Strangely, fans seem to love the game even more because of it.

o: In a tavern full of thieves
On a cart with other prisoners
On top of a snowy mountain

o: He can use dragon words as magical shouts

title: GTA V: Three Criminals and One Big City
ru: GTA V: три героя, огромный город Лос-Сантос и GTA Online
text:
In September 2013, a video game earned a billion dollars in just three days — faster than any film or game before it. That game was Grand Theft Auto V, and more than ten years later it is still one of the best-selling games of all time.

GTA V was developed by Rockstar North, a studio in Edinburgh, Scotland, and published by Rockstar Games. It's a little funny that a game about sunny California was created in a city famous for its rain.

The game takes place in Los Santos, a fictional version of Los Angeles, and the countryside around it. There are beaches, Hollywood-style hills, poor neighbourhoods, deserts and a mountain you can jump off with a parachute. The city feels alive: people jog, argue, take selfies and call the police when you do something stupid — which happens a lot.

For the first time in the series, you control three main characters. Michael is a retired bank robber with a big house, an unhappy family and far too much free time. Franklin is a young man from the streets who wants something better than small crimes. And Trevor is Michael's old partner — loud, wild and completely unpredictable. You can switch between them at almost any moment, and you never know what you'll find. Sometimes Trevor wakes up somewhere strange in his underwear, with no idea how he got there.

The best missions are the heists — big, carefully planned robberies. Before each one, you choose your plan and your team. A cheap driver might crash the getaway car; an expensive hacker gives you more time inside. These decisions really change how the mission goes.

The game is also a satire: it makes fun of American culture, social media, celebrities and advertising, with fake radio shows and adverts that are often hilarious. However, it's definitely a game for adults, with a lot of violence and strong language.

Then there's GTA Online, the multiplayer mode, which Rockstar has kept updating for years. It's one of the reasons why GTA V has been released on three generations of consoles. For years, fans waited for any news about GTA VI — and many of them kept playing GTA V the whole time.

title: Dota 2: Five Against Five
ru: Как устроена Dota 2 и почему её турниры смотрят миллионы
text:
In 2021, five young players from Team Spirit, a team from the CIS, sat on a stage in Bucharest and won more than eighteen million dollars. They weren't playing football or tennis. They were playing Dota 2.

Dota 2 is a free online game from Valve, an American company, and it was released in 2013. But its story began years earlier, as a fan project. Defense of the Ancients, or DotA, was a custom map for the strategy game Warcraft III, created and improved by fans. One of its main developers, known only by his online name, IceFrog, later joined Valve and led the work on Dota 2.

The rules sound simple. Two teams of five, the Radiant and the Dire, fight on one map. Each side has a large building called the Ancient. Destroy the enemy's Ancient, and you win. Every player controls one hero, chosen from more than a hundred, and each hero has their own skills. A match usually lasts thirty to fifty minutes.

In practice, though, Dota 2 is famously hard. You need to know what every hero can do, buy the right items at the right moment and work closely with four other people — who might be strangers who don't even speak your language. One mistake can lose the whole game, which is why Dota players are known for being passionate and, let's say, very emotional in the chat.

Dota 2 is also one of the giants of esports — professional gaming competitions where teams train like athletes and play in front of huge crowds. The biggest event is The International, held since 2011. For a long time, part of the money that fans spent on in-game items was added to its prize pool, so the prizes grew enormous. In 2021, the total prize pool was over forty million dollars, more than in many traditional sports tournaments.

Teams from Europe, China, North America and the CIS have all lifted the Aegis of Champions, the famous trophy shaped like a shield. Team Spirit won it again in 2023.

You don't need to play to enjoy it. Watch one final with good commentators, and you might finally understand why millions of people shout at their screens.

o: As a fan-made map for Warcraft III
As a sports game made by Valve
As a card game for professional players

o: By collecting more than a hundred heroes
By staying alive for fifty minutes

questions.q: Why did the prizes at The International become so big?
o: Valve sold tickets at very high prices
Football clubs paid for the tournament

title: Speedrunning: Finishing Games Very, Very Fast
ru: Что такое спидраны и почему люди проходят игры за минуты
text:
The original Super Mario Bros. came out in 1985, and most children who played it needed weeks to reach the end. Today, the fastest players in the world finish it in under five minutes — and they still fight for every hundredth of a second. Welcome to speedrunning: the art of finishing games as fast as humanly possible.

How do they do it? The first secret is practice, and a lot of it. Top runners have played the same game thousands of times. They know the shortest route through every level and exactly when to jump, often down to a single frame. A frame is one of the still pictures that make up the moving image, and many games show sixty of them every second. Being one frame late can ruin a whole run.

The second secret is glitches — mistakes in a game's code. A good glitch might let a player walk through a wall, skip half a level or jump straight to the final boss. Runners spend months hunting for new tricks, and when someone finds one, the world record can suddenly drop by several minutes. Then everyone has to learn the new trick, or fall behind.

Speedruns are divided into categories. In “any%”, anything is allowed as long as you reach the end. In “100%”, you have to collect everything first. Some categories ban the biggest glitches, so the run stays closer to normal play. Records are collected on sites like speedrun.com, where moderators check every new record before it is accepted.

Speedrunning has also become something people love to watch. Games Done Quick is a week-long marathon in the USA, held twice a year, where runners play live while viewers donate money. Over the years, these events have raised tens of millions of dollars for charities such as Doctors Without Borders.

But the best part is the drama. Imagine a runner who has been on record pace for forty minutes and then falls into a hole right before the finish. Thousands of viewers groan at the same moment. It's a strange sport — but it is a sport, with all the pain and glory that comes with it.

Is there a game you know by heart? If so, you might already be halfway to your first speedrun.

title: Small Teams, Big Hits: Hollow Knight and Stardew Valley
ru: Две инди-игры, которые сделали крошечные команды, а полюбил весь мир
text:
Stardew Valley was made by one man. Not one studio — one man. Eric Barone, known online as ConcernedApe, spent about four and a half years writing the code, drawing every character, composing the music and writing the story himself. When the game finally came out in 2016, it became a huge hit.

In Stardew Valley, you leave a grey office job at a big corporation and move to your late grandfather's old farm near Pelican Town. Then you do whatever you want: plant vegetables, raise chickens, go fishing, explore a mine full of slimes, or make friends — and maybe fall in love — with the people in town. Barone was inspired by the Harvest Moon farming games he had loved as a child, but he added more characters, more secrets and a lot of warmth. Many players say it's the perfect game for the end of a stressful day.

Hollow Knight, released in 2017, is a very different kind of game. It was made by Team Cherry, a tiny studio from Adelaide, Australia, with a core team of just three people. They raised their first money through Kickstarter, a website where fans pay to support a project they believe in.

You play as a small, silent knight armed with a nail instead of a sword, exploring Hallownest, a ruined underground kingdom of insects. The world is beautiful, sad and full of hidden paths. It is also hard: bosses will beat you again and again until you learn every one of their moves. When you finally win, it feels amazing.

Fans loved Hollow Knight so much that the wait for its sequel, Hollow Knight: Silksong, became a running joke online. Every time a big gaming show was announced, people hoped for news, and almost every time, there was nothing. Silksong finally came out in 2025, more than six years after it was first announced.

On the surface, a calm farm and a dark insect kingdom have nothing in common. But both games prove the same thing: you don't need a huge team or a huge budget to build a world that millions of people want to live in. You need talent, patience and a lot of love.

title: Elden Ring: Hard, Beautiful and Unforgettable
ru: Elden Ring: сложная, но честная игра с огромным открытым миром
text:
Imagine a game where you die over and over again — and you keep coming back for more. Millions of people have done exactly that with Elden Ring.

Elden Ring was released in 2022 by FromSoftware, a Japanese studio famous for the Dark Souls series and for games that don't forgive mistakes. It was directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki, and George R. R. Martin, the author of the books behind Game of Thrones, helped to create the ancient history of its world. The same year, it won Game of the Year at The Game Awards.

You play as one of the Tarnished, exiled warriors who return to a land called the Lands Between. This place was once ruled by gods and queens, but the Elden Ring, the source of its order, has been shattered, and now the land is broken, beautiful and dangerous. Like other FromSoftware games, Elden Ring doesn't explain its story directly. Instead, you piece it together from item descriptions, strange conversations and the ruins you pass on your way. Fans have spent years arguing about what it all means.

The big change was the open world. You can ride your spirit horse, Torrent, almost anywhere. If a boss is too strong, you're free to leave, explore another area, get stronger and come back later. This freedom made the game much more welcoming than earlier FromSoftware titles.

Don't worry, though: it's still hard. Some bosses can defeat you fifty times in one evening. Margit, one of the first serious bosses, has stopped countless new players for hours. But when you finally beat an enemy that has been destroying you all night, the feeling is incredible.

One of the game's most charming features is the message system. Players can leave short notes on the ground for others, built from a list of ready-made words. Some messages are genuinely helpful, like a warning about a hidden trap. Others say “Try jumping” right next to a cliff. You quickly learn not to trust everyone.

In 2024, a large expansion called Shadow of the Erdtree was released, and it was even tougher. If you are patient, curious and not afraid of dying, Elden Ring might become the most memorable game you have ever played.

title: Spirited Away: A Girl in the World of Spirits
ru: «Унесённые призраками» Миядзаки и история студии Ghibli
text:
For almost twenty years, the most successful film in the history of Japanese cinema was not a samurai epic or a Hollywood blockbuster. It was a hand-drawn cartoon about a ten-year-old girl who works in a bathhouse for spirits.

Spirited Away came out in 2001. It was written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki and made by Studio Ghibli, which Miyazaki had founded in 1985 together with the director Isao Takahata and the producer Toshio Suzuki. Ghibli was already loved in Japan for films like My Neighbor Totoro and Princess Mononoke, but Spirited Away took it to the whole world.

The story begins with a boring car journey. Chihiro is moving to a new town with her parents, and she is sulking — sitting in the back seat, silent and unhappy. Her father takes a wrong turn, and the family finds what looks like an abandoned theme park. There is hot food on the counters, but nobody to sell it. Her parents start eating anyway — and they turn into pigs. As the sun goes down, the spirits come out, and Chihiro is alone.

To survive and save her parents, she has to get a job in a huge bathhouse where gods and spirits come to wash and relax. It is run by Yubaba, a witch with an enormous head and a terrible temper, who takes away Chihiro's name and calls her Sen. In this world, if you forget your real name, you can forget who you are.

The bathhouse is full of unforgettable characters: Kamaji, an old man with many long arms who runs the boiler room; the tiny soot balls that carry coal; and No-Face, a silent, lonely spirit in a mask who becomes dangerous when he gets too much attention. Little by little, the scared, spoiled girl becomes brave, hard-working and kind.

Spirited Away won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature, and it was the first anime ever to do so. It remained Japan's highest-grossing film until 2020, when Demon Slayer: Mugen Train finally beat it.

Watch it once as a fairy tale. Then watch it again and look at the small details — they are everywhere.

title: Naruto: The Boy Nobody Believed In
ru: Naruto: история мальчика-ниндзя, который хотел, чтобы его признали
text:
Here's a strange fact to start with: in Japanese, naruto is also the name of a fish cake with a pink swirl, a common topping in ramen. That fits perfectly, because the hero of Naruto loves ramen more than almost anything in the world.

Naruto began as a manga by Masashi Kishimoto, published in the magazine Weekly Shonen Jump from 1999 to 2014. The anime started in 2002, and it continued in 2007 with Naruto Shippuden, which follows an older Naruto. Together, the two series have hundreds of episodes.

Naruto Uzumaki lives in the Hidden Leaf Village. He is loud, cheeky and always playing tricks — in the very first episode, he paints all over the giant stone faces of the village's great leaders. But behind the jokes, he is very lonely. He has no parents, and the adults of the village look at him with cold eyes. The reason is a secret that he doesn't know at first: when he was a baby, a monster called the Nine-Tailed Fox was sealed inside his body. People see the monster, not the boy.

Naruto has one big dream: to become Hokage, the leader and strongest ninja of the village, so that everyone will finally have to respect him. The problem is that he is the worst student in his class. He fails exams and can barely perform the basic techniques. However, he has one talent nobody can teach: he never, ever gives up.

He joins Team 7 with Sasuke, a cold genius who wants revenge for his family, and Sakura, a smart girl who has a crush on Sasuke. Their teacher, Kakashi, is a relaxed ninja who is always late and always reading the same little orange book. The friendship and rivalry between Naruto and Sasuke drives the whole story.

Why has Naruto become so popular all over the world? The fights are exciting, of course, but the heart of the series is simpler. Most people have felt like outsiders at some point. Watching Naruto slowly win the respect of the people who once ignored him feels like a small victory for all of us.

The series is long, but the first episodes are some of the funniest. Just be warned: you may suddenly want a big bowl of ramen.

title: Attack on Titan: Life Behind the Walls
ru: Attack on Titan: мрачное аниме о людях за стенами и тайне титанов
text:
For a hundred years, humanity has lived safely behind three enormous walls. Outside, giants walk the land. Inside, people farm, trade, drink and argue — and most of them have forgotten what fear feels like. Then, one ordinary afternoon, a head appears over the top of the outer wall. It is sixty metres tall, and it has no skin.

That's how Attack on Titan begins, and it's one of the most famous opening episodes in anime. The story was created by the Japanese artist Hajime Isayama. His manga ran from 2009 to 2021, and the anime from 2013 to 2023. The first three seasons were animated by Wit Studio, and the final season by MAPPA.

The giants are called Titans. They look like naked humans with strange, empty smiles; they can't speak, and they eat people. Nobody knows where they came from or why they attack. When the Colossal Titan breaks a hole in the wall, a boy named Eren Yeager loses his home and his mother in a single day. He swears to destroy every Titan in the world.

Together with his friends Mikasa, a quiet girl who is an incredible fighter, and Armin, a shy boy with a brilliant mind, Eren joins the Survey Corps — the soldiers who go outside the walls to fight Titans and find out the truth about them. They fly between trees and buildings using special gear with steel cables and gas, aiming for the back of a Titan's neck, its only weak spot. The show also gave fans one of anime's most popular characters, Captain Levi, a short, serious soldier who is obsessed with cleaning.

At first, it seems like a simple story of humans against monsters. It isn't. Every season reveals something that changes how you see the earlier ones. Without spoilers, the series grows into a story about freedom and war, and about how ordinary people can become monsters too. Characters you trusted may surprise you, and fans still argue about who was right.

Be warned: Attack on Titan is violent and often heartbreaking, and important characters can die at any moment. But if you enjoy serious stories with real mysteries, few anime are as powerful.

title: One Piece: The Longest Adventure
ru: One Piece: пираты, дружба и приключение длиной в десятилетия
text:
In 1997, a young Japanese artist named Eiichiro Oda started a manga about a boy who wanted to become the King of the Pirates. He expected it to last about five years. Almost three decades later, the story is still going.

One Piece is published in the magazine Weekly Shonen Jump, and its anime, made by Toei Animation, began in 1999. In 2015, it set a Guinness World Record for the most copies published of a comic series by a single author, and by 2022 more than five hundred million copies had been printed around the world.

The hero is Monkey D. Luffy, a cheerful, always hungry and very stubborn young man in a straw hat. As a child, he ate a Devil Fruit, a mysterious fruit that gives strange powers, and his body turned into rubber. He can stretch his arms like elastic and throw a punch from across a room. There's one catch: anyone who eats a Devil Fruit can never swim again. For a pirate, that's not ideal.

Luffy is searching for the One Piece, a legendary treasure left by the last King of the Pirates. On the way, he gathers a crew of misfits — people who don't fit in anywhere else — called the Straw Hat Pirates. There's Zoro, a swordsman who fights with three swords — one held in his mouth — and gets lost everywhere he goes; Nami, a navigator who loves money; Sanji, a cook who fights only with his legs to protect his hands; and Usopp, a sniper and a terrible liar. Later, even a talking reindeer who works as a doctor joins them.

At first, One Piece looks silly: bright colours, crazy faces, ridiculous fights. But behind the jokes, it deals with serious topics like slavery, injustice and the abuse of power. Each crew member carries a painful past, and many fans admit they have cried at scenes they expected to be just funny. The bond between the crew is the heart of the story.

The only problem is the length: the anime has well over a thousand episodes. If that sounds scary, try the 2023 live-action series on Netflix, which tells the beginning of the story in eight episodes. Or just start the anime and see how far the waves carry you.

title: How Pixar Was Born
ru: Как небольшой компьютерный отдел превратился в Pixar и сделал «Историю игрушек»
text:
In 1979, George Lucas had just made Star Wars, and he wanted computers to help him make films. So his company, Lucasfilm, hired a small group of scientists to work on the future of cinema. Nobody knew it yet, but that little team would one day become Pixar.

One of its leaders was Ed Catmull, a computer scientist who had dreamed since his student days of making a whole film on a computer. In the early 1980s, the team was joined by John Lasseter, a young animator who had just lost his job at Disney — partly because he was too excited about computer animation.

In 1986, Lucas decided to sell the group. The buyer was Steve Jobs, who had recently been pushed out of Apple, the company he had co-founded. The group became an independent company called Pixar. The name came from a made-up word that was supposed to sound like a Spanish verb meaning “to make pictures”.

Here's the surprising part: Pixar wasn't planning to make films. It was a hardware company that sold an expensive machine, the Pixar Image Computer, and for years it lost money. Jobs kept paying to keep it alive. To show what their technology could do, the team made short films. The first, Luxo Jr. (1986), was about two desk lamps, a parent and a child, playing with a ball. That little jumping lamp later became the studio's logo. A few years later, Pixar's short Tin Toy became the first computer-animated film to win an Oscar.

Then Disney agreed to work with Pixar on a full-length film. In 1995, Toy Story came out — the first feature film made entirely with computer animation. The story of Woody, a cowboy doll, and Buzz Lightyear, a space toy who doesn't know he's a toy, made children laugh and adults cry. It became the most successful film of the year in America.

After that came hit after hit: Monsters, Inc., Finding Nemo, The Incredibles, Up, Inside Out. In 2006, Disney bought Pixar, and Steve Jobs became Disney's largest shareholder.

So next time you see that little lamp hop across the screen before a film, remember: it started as a test, made by a few engineers and artists who refused to give up.

title: From Teacher to Criminal
ru: Как скромный учитель химии стал героем одного из лучших сериалов в истории
text:
Before Breaking Bad, most viewers knew Bryan Cranston as Hal, the silly dad from the comedy Malcolm in the Middle. Then he shaved his head, put on a pair of glasses and became Walter White — one of the most frightening characters in TV history.

Breaking Bad was created by Vince Gilligan and ran on the American channel AMC from 2008 to 2013, for five seasons. Gilligan once summed up the idea in one sentence: he wanted to turn Mr. Chips into Scarface — in other words, to take a gentle, ordinary teacher and slowly turn him into a gangster.

Walter White teaches chemistry at a high school in Albuquerque, New Mexico. He is brilliant but badly paid, and he has a second job at a car wash, where he sometimes has to clean his own students' cars. Soon after his fiftieth birthday, he learns that he is seriously ill and may not have long to live. Afraid of leaving his family with nothing, he decides to use his chemistry skills to make illegal drugs. His partner is Jesse Pinkman, a former student who is now a small-time dealer.

What makes the show special is the transformation. In the first season, you feel sorry for Walter. As the seasons go on, he becomes proud, cold and dangerous, and he even takes a new name: Heisenberg. You keep watching because you need to know how far he will go. Aaron Paul, who plays Jesse, gives the show its heart: Jesse makes plenty of bad decisions, but unlike Walter, he never stops feeling guilty about them.

There's a funny real-life story connected to the show. In one famous scene, Walter angrily throws a whole pizza onto the roof of his house. The real house is in Albuquerque, and for years, fans came to throw pizzas onto its roof. In the end, Vince Gilligan had to ask them publicly to stop.

The show also looks amazing: endless desert, bright yellow protective suits, long silent scenes that feel like an old western. If you finish it and want more, there's Better Call Saul, a spin-off about Walter's lawyer, which many fans think is just as good.

title: The Fight for the Iron Throne
ru: Фэнтези-сериал HBO о борьбе знатных семей за власть в Вестеросе
text:
“Winter is coming.” For eight seasons, the motto of the Stark family was a warning that the characters kept ignoring and viewers took very seriously.

Game of Thrones ran on the American channel HBO from 2011 to 2019. It was created by David Benioff and D. B. Weiss and based on A Song of Ice and Fire, a series of fantasy novels by George R. R. Martin. By the end, it had won 59 Emmy awards, more than any other drama series in history.

The story takes place in Westeros, an imaginary land that looks a lot like medieval Europe — except for the dragons, the walking dead and the summers and winters that can last for years. Several great families, including the honourable Starks and the rich, clever Lannisters, fight for the Iron Throne, a seat made from the melted swords of defeated enemies. Across the sea, Daenerys Targaryen, the last daughter of an old royal family, is trying to win back her family's crown, and she has something nobody else in the world has: three baby dragons. And far in the north, behind a huge wall of ice, an ancient danger is waking up.

What shocked viewers most was that nobody was safe. In most fantasy stories, the hero survives. In Game of Thrones, main characters could die suddenly, sometimes in the very first season. People began watching new episodes with their hands over their mouths.

The characters are not simply good or bad, either. Tyrion Lannister, a sharp-tongued man whose own family looks down on him, became a fan favourite thanks to his jokes and his intelligence. Heroes make terrible mistakes, while some villains become strangely likeable.

The show was filmed in real places: Northern Ireland, Croatia, Spain, Iceland and Malta. The old city of Dubrovnik in Croatia played King's Landing, the capital, and its streets are now full of tourists asking where exactly a certain scene was shot.

Not everyone liked the final season, and people still argue about it online. But Game of Thrones changed television: it proved that a TV series could be as big, expensive and exciting as a Hollywood film. If you miss Westeros, the prequel House of the Dragon began in 2022.

title: Children's Games, Adult Rules
ru: Южнокорейский сериал о людях в долгах, которые играют в детские игры ради огромного приза
text:
Hwang Dong-hyuk wrote the first version of Squid Game in 2008. For about ten years, nobody wanted it: producers thought the story was too strange and too violent. When Netflix finally released it in September 2021, it quickly became the most-watched series in the platform's history up to that time.

The main character, Seong Gi-hun, is a likeable loser. He is deep in debt, he gambles on horse races, and he even takes money from his own mother. One day, a stranger in a suit offers him a game at a train station: play ddakji, a Korean game with folded paper squares, and win money for every round. Lose, and get slapped in the face. Soon Gi-hun is invited to a secret competition on a hidden island. There are 456 players, all of them in serious financial trouble, and the prize is 45.6 billion won — tens of millions of dollars.

The games are simple children's games, like Red Light, Green Light, played in front of a giant doll with a sweet face. The rules are the same as in childhood. The difference is what happens to those who lose.

The look of the show is unforgettable: players in green tracksuits with numbers on them, guards in pink jumpsuits with circles, triangles and squares on their masks, and huge rooms that look like colourful playgrounds. The contrast between bright, childish colours and terrible events is what makes it so disturbing. After the show came out, people around the world tried the dalgona challenge, carefully cutting a shape out of a thin, crunchy sugar candy with a needle.

But Squid Game is more than a thriller. It asks hard questions about money, inequality and what people are willing to do when they feel they have no other choice. Some players become cruel; others show surprising kindness.

Lee Jung-jae, who plays Gi-hun, won the Emmy for best lead actor in a drama in 2022, the first Asian actor ever to do so. The story continued in a second season in 2024 and ended with a third in 2025.

Just maybe don't watch it right before a family games night.

title: The Dark Side of Technology
ru: Британский сериал-антология о том, как технологии могут изменить нашу жизнь
text:
Turn off your phone and look at the screen. That dark, shiny rectangle reflecting your face is the “black mirror” that gave this series its name. Its creator, the British writer Charlie Brooker, has said that this is exactly what he had in mind.

Black Mirror started on the UK's Channel 4 in 2011 and moved to Netflix in 2016, where it found a global audience. It's an anthology series: every episode tells a completely separate story, with new characters, a new world and sometimes a new genre. One episode is a horror film, another is a love story, another is a dark comedy. What connects them is one question: what happens when technology gives people exactly what they want?

The ideas are usually just one small step away from today, and that's what makes them frightening. In “Nosedive”, people rate each other from one to five stars after every conversation, and your score decides where you can live and who will talk to you. The heroine is desperate to raise her rating, and you can almost feel her fake smile hurting her face. In “The Entire History of You”, a tiny device behind the ear records everything you see, so couples can replay every argument they have ever had. That sounds useful — until you realise you can never forget anything.

Not every episode is dark, though. “San Junipero”, about two women who meet in a seaside town in the 1980s, is warm, mysterious and deeply moving. It won an Emmy and is often called the best episode of the whole series. In 2018, the creators also made Bandersnatch, an interactive film in which viewers use their remote control to choose what the main character does next. Some choices lead to a happy ending; many don't.

Because every story is separate, you can watch Black Mirror in any order. A good plan is to start with one of the famous episodes, see how you feel, and then decide how deep you want to go.

One warning: after a few episodes, you may start looking at your phone a little differently — and maybe even put it face down on the table.

title: The Doctor Nobody Likes
ru: Медицинская драма о гениальном, но очень трудном докторе Хаусе
text:
“Everybody lies.” That's the first rule of Dr Gregory House, and it explains a lot about him. He doesn't trust his patients, he doesn't trust his team, and he certainly doesn't trust his boss. The annoying thing is that he is usually right.

House M.D. is an American medical drama that ran on Fox from 2004 to 2012, for eight seasons. It was created by David Shore. At its peak, it was watched all over the planet: in 2008, Guinness World Records named it the most-watched TV programme in the world, with tens of millions of viewers in more than sixty countries.

House leads a small team of doctors at Princeton-Plainsboro, a hospital in New Jersey. They only take the cases that no other doctor can explain. A typical episode is really a detective story. The team writes the symptoms on a whiteboard, tries one idea after another, gets it wrong, gets it wrong again — and then House notices a tiny detail, often while talking about something completely different, and suddenly knows the answer.

As a person, though, House is a nightmare. He is rude, sarcastic and lazy. He avoids patients whenever he can and hides from the clinic where he is supposed to work. He walks with a cane because of a painful problem with his leg, and he swallows painkillers like sweets. His only real friend is Dr James Wilson, a kind oncologist — a cancer doctor — who somehow stays loyal to him.

If this sounds familiar, you're right: House was inspired by Sherlock Holmes. Holmes has Watson; House has Wilson. Holmes lives at 221B Baker Street; House lives in apartment 221B. Fans also love one running joke: whenever someone suggests lupus, a rare disease, as the answer, someone else reminds them that it is never lupus.

One more surprise: Hugh Laurie, who plays House, is British. He recorded his audition video in a hotel bathroom while he was filming in Africa, and his American accent was so convincing that one of the show's producers reportedly thought he was American.

If you like clever puzzles and sharp dialogue, House is a perfect show to binge — that is, to watch one episode after another until it's suddenly 3 a.m.

title: Stranded on a Strange Island
ru: Загадочный сериал о пассажирах самолёта, оказавшихся на таинственном острове
text:
In 2004, the American channel ABC spent more than ten million dollars on a single pilot episode, one of the most expensive in TV history at that time. The result was a spectacular plane crash on a tropical beach — and the start of Lost, one of the most talked-about series of the 2000s.

Lost ran from 2004 to 2010, for six seasons. It was created by J. J. Abrams, Damon Lindelof and Jeffrey Lieber, and it won the Emmy for best drama series after its very first season.

The story begins seconds after Oceanic Flight 815 breaks apart in the air over the Pacific Ocean. Dozens of passengers survive and find themselves on an island. They wait for rescue, but nobody comes. Soon they notice that this is not a normal island. Something huge moves through the jungle, knocking down trees. There is a polar bear — on a tropical island. And a strange set of numbers keeps appearing in the most unexpected places: 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42.

The survivors are a mix of very different people: Jack, a doctor who doesn't really want to be a leader; Kate, who is clearly hiding something about her past; Sawyer, a sarcastic con man — a professional cheat — who reads novels on the beach; and John Locke, a quiet man who believes the island has a plan for them. Each episode includes flashbacks to one character's life before the crash, and slowly you learn that almost nobody on that plane was who they seemed to be.

But the real star was the mystery. Each episode answered one question and asked two new ones. Fans built huge websites full of theories, and the next morning at work, everyone wanted to discuss what they had seen. Long before streaming made binge-watching normal, Lost turned TV into a weekly puzzle that viewers all over the world tried to solve together.

The show was filmed on Oahu, an island in Hawaii, so the beaches and jungle you see on screen are real — and beautiful.

The ending divided fans, and some still complain that too many questions were never answered. But if a series today makes you search for theories online after every episode, it probably owes something to Lost.

title: Caps, Coats and Family Business
ru: Британская драма о семье Шелби и бандитском Бирмингеме после Первой мировой войны
text:
Birmingham, 1919. Smoke from the factories hangs over dirty streets, and men who survived the First World War are trying to live with what they saw there. Then a man on a black horse rides slowly through the crowd, and everyone steps out of his way. This is Tommy Shelby, and this is Peaky Blinders.

The British crime drama was created by Steven Knight and first shown on the BBC in 2013. It ran for six series, ending in 2022, and became a worldwide hit thanks to Netflix.

The Shelbys are a working-class family who run a gang called the Peaky Blinders. They take illegal bets on horse races, fight rival gangs and make deals with very dangerous people. According to legend, the gang's men sewed razor blades into the peaks of their flat caps and used them as weapons. Historians aren't sure that's true, but it makes a great story.

Tommy, the head of the family, came back from the war with nightmares and a cold, calculating mind. He wants to turn a small street business into a real empire, and he always seems to be three steps ahead of his enemies. He is played by the Irish actor Cillian Murphy, who later won an Oscar for Oppenheimer. Murphy plays Tommy with very few words: a long look, a cigarette, one quiet sentence — and you understand exactly how dangerous he is.

The family around him is just as memorable. His older brother Arthur is wild and violent but has a good heart under all that anger. His aunt Polly, played by Helen McCrory, is sharp, wise and afraid of nobody; she ran the family business while the men were away at war.

The show's style became famous around the world. Men copied the haircuts, very short at the sides, along with the long coats and flat caps. The music is unusual too: instead of songs from the 1920s, the series uses modern rock, starting with its theme song, “Red Right Hand” by Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds. It shouldn't work, but it does.

Even if you've never liked historical dramas, give Peaky Blinders one episode. By the end, you may catch yourself saying, in a low voice, “By order of the Peaky Blinders.”

title: A Small Town with a Big Secret
ru: Немецкий сериал о путешествиях во времени и тайнах маленького городка
text:
In the small German town of Winden, children have a habit of disappearing. In 2019, a boy goes missing in the forest near some old caves. Thirty-three years earlier, in 1986, another boy disappeared in the same place. As the people of Winden start to search, they slowly realise that the real question is not where the children went — but when.

Dark was created by Baran bo Odar and Jantje Friese. It was Netflix's first original series from Germany, and it ran from 2017 to 2020 in three seasons. The creators planned it from the start as one complete story with a fixed ending, which is rare for television.

The main character is Jonas Kahnwald, a teenager in a yellow raincoat whose father has recently died. Jonas wants to understand why. The more he digs, the more he discovers that the past, the present and the future of Winden are tied together like a knot. Important events seem to repeat every 33 years, and four families — the Kahnwalds, the Nielsens, the Dopplers and the Tiedemanns — turn out to be connected in ways that become more shocking with every episode.

Dark is not a show you can watch while scrolling through your phone. The same character can appear as a child, an adult and an old person, played by different actors, and you have to remember who is who. Many fans drew family trees on paper to keep up, and Netflix even made an official interactive guide to help confused viewers. Some people watched the whole series twice and noticed details the second time that they had completely missed before.

But this is exactly what makes it so rewarding. When a tiny detail from the first season suddenly makes sense in the third, it feels like solving a puzzle you have been working on for weeks. The mood helps too: endless rain, dark forests, a nuclear power plant on the edge of town and slow, haunting music.

If you decide to watch Dark, try the original German version with subtitles; the real voices fit the atmosphere much better. And keep a notebook nearby. You'll need it.

title: A Game That Became Great TV
ru: Как видеоигра превратилась в один из лучших сериалов HBO
text:
There is a real fungus called Cordyceps that can take control of an insect's body, make it climb up a plant and then kill it. It sounds like a horror film. In The Last of Us, it is one: the fungus learns to infect humans, and the world falls apart.

The HBO series first appeared in January 2023. It was created by Craig Mazin, who had already made the highly praised miniseries Chernobyl, and Neil Druckmann, who wrote and co-directed the original 2013 video game at the studio Naughty Dog. For years, people had said that games could never become good TV. This show proved them wrong.

Most of the story takes place twenty years after the outbreak. The survivors live in guarded quarantine zones, controlled by a strict military government, while infected people wander through the ruins outside. Joel, a tough, quiet man who lost his daughter on the first night of the disaster, gets a job he doesn't want: to smuggle a fourteen-year-old girl named Ellie across the country. Ellie has a secret that could change the world, though at first Joel has no idea why she matters so much.

Joel is played by Pedro Pascal and Ellie by Bella Ramsey, and the relationship between them is the heart of the show. At first, Joel treats Ellie like a package to be delivered, and she treats him like a grumpy old man. She reads him terrible jokes from a joke book; he tries very hard not to laugh. Slowly, almost without noticing, they become a family.

Surprisingly, the infected aren't on screen all that often. The show is more interested in people: how they survive, what they lose, and what they are willing to do for the ones they love. The third episode, “Long, Long Time”, almost forgets about the main plot and tells the love story of two other survivors, Bill and Frank, across many years. Critics called it one of the best TV episodes of the year, and Nick Offerman won an Emmy for playing Bill.

A second season followed in 2025. If you have played the game, you'll recognise many scenes, sometimes shot by shot. If you haven't, it doesn't matter — just keep some tissues nearby.

title: Two Sisters, Two Cities
ru: Анимационный сериал по вселенной League of Legends о двух сёстрах — Вай и Джинкс
text:
When Arcane was announced, many people expected just a long advert for a video game. Instead, it became one of the most praised animated series of its time — and plenty of its fans have never played League of Legends at all.

Arcane was made by the game company Riot Games together with Fortiche, an animation studio from Paris. The first season appeared on Netflix in November 2021, and the second and final season followed in 2024. Making the show took about six years.

The story is set in two cities, one directly above the other, that live in completely different worlds. Piltover, on top, is rich, clean and full of inventors, golden towers and polite council meetings. Zaun, the undercity below, is poor, polluted and run by criminals. Vi and her little sister Powder are orphans from Zaun. Vi is tough and protective and solves problems with her fists. Powder desperately wants to be useful, but her homemade inventions keep going wrong. After one terrible night, the sisters are separated, and Powder slowly becomes Jinx — a brilliant, unstable girl with a love of explosions.

Meanwhile, in Piltover, a young scientist named Jayce and his friend Viktor are trying to combine science and magic. Their discovery could change everything for both cities, for better or for worse.

The first thing that surprises viewers is the look. Fortiche mixes 3D animation with hand-painted textures, so every frame looks like a moving painting. Faces show tiny emotions: a tired look, a forced smile, a second of doubt. The fights are fast and stylish, but the quiet scenes between the two sisters hit even harder.

The music matters too. The opening song, “Enemy” by Imagine Dragons, became a huge hit and stayed stuck in people's heads for months.

In 2022, Arcane became the first streaming series to win the Emmy for Outstanding Animated Program. More importantly, it showed many adults that animation isn't only for children. At its core, this is a story about family, loss and inequality, and about how someone can become a villain step by step, almost without noticing.

If you think you don't like cartoons, Arcane might be the show that changes your mind.

title: The Perfect Robbery Plan
about: Money Heist / La casa de papel (2017–2021)
ru: Испанский сериал о группе грабителей в красных комбинезонах и их гениальном Профессоре
text:
Most robbers want to steal money. The robbers in Money Heist have a stranger idea: they want to make it. Their plan is to lock themselves inside the Royal Mint of Spain, the building where the country prints its banknotes, and print billions of euros of their own.

The Spanish series, whose original title is La casa de papel (“The House of Paper”), was created by Álex Pina and first appeared on the TV channel Antena 3 in 2017. In Spain it was a modest success, nothing more. Then Netflix bought it, cut it into shorter episodes and showed it to the whole world. Almost overnight, a Spanish crime show became one of the most-watched non-English series on the platform.

The gang is led by a quiet, polite man known only as the Professor. He has spent years preparing every detail, and he never enters the building himself. Instead, he controls the heist from a hidden room outside, talking to the police on the phone while secretly working against them. The robbers inside are not allowed to use their real names or talk about their private lives, so they choose the names of cities: Tokyo, Berlin, Nairobi, Rio, Denver, Moscow. Tokyo tells the story, so we see everything through her eyes.

The look of the gang has become famous far beyond the show. They wear red jumpsuits and masks with the face of the painter Salvador Dalí, the artist with the long, curly moustache. Since the show became a hit, people have worn the same costume at Halloween parties, football matches and even street protests. The old Italian song “Bella ciao”, which the characters sing at important moments, also became a hit again thanks to the series.

What keeps viewers watching is the tension. The plan looks perfect on paper, but people are not machines. The robbers argue, panic, fall in love and break the Professor's rules, and every mistake forces him to improvise.

If you enjoy it, there is more: a Korean remake set in a future where North and South Korea are about to unite, and a spin-off about Berlin, the most charming and most dangerous member of the gang.

title: A Queen's Life on Screen
ru: Историческая драма о жизни королевы Елизаветы II и британской королевской семьи
text:
Imagine becoming the head of a country at the age of twenty-five, without ever asking for the job. That is where The Crown begins. Princess Elizabeth is a young wife and mother, happily married to Prince Philip, when her father, King George VI, dies in 1952. Overnight, she becomes Queen Elizabeth II, and her private life is never really private again.

The series was created by the British writer Peter Morgan, who had already written about the Queen in the film The Queen and the stage play The Audience. Netflix released it in 2016, and over six seasons it followed the royal family from the late 1940s to the early 2000s. Each season mixes big historical events, such as political crises and royal weddings, with quiet scenes behind closed doors that no journalist ever saw.

The show's cleverest trick is its casting. Because the story covers more than fifty years, the main actors were replaced every two seasons. Claire Foy played the young Queen, Olivia Colman played her in middle age, and Imelda Staunton played her in her later years. Prince Philip, Princess Margaret and the other main characters were recast in the same way. At first this sounds strange, but it works: you really feel that time has passed and that the characters have grown older.

The series was also famous for its budget and its attention to detail. Costumes, palaces, cars and even royal dinners were recreated with great care, and The Crown became one of the most expensive TV dramas ever made. It won many awards, including several Emmys.

However, it is important to remember that The Crown is a drama, not a documentary. Nobody knows exactly what the Queen said to her prime ministers in private, so many conversations are imagined by the writer. Some viewers and politicians complained that people might believe the invented scenes were real, and they asked Netflix to make clear that the show is fiction.

Even so, if you want to hear beautiful British English and understand why the royal family fascinates so many people, The Crown is a great place to start.

title: Succession: A Family at War Over an Empire
ru: Почему драма о богатой семье, делящей медиаимперию, стала одним из главных сериалов десятилетия
text:
Imagine that your father owns half the news you watch, and he has just asked you to prove you deserve his love in front of the board of directors. That, more or less, is every family dinner in Succession, the HBO drama that ran for four seasons between 2018 and 2023 and turned a group of thoroughly unpleasant billionaires into some of the most compelling characters on television.

Created by the British writer Jesse Armstrong, the show follows the Roy family, owners of a giant media and entertainment company called Waystar Royco. At the top sits Logan Roy, played by Brian Cox, an ageing tycoon who rules his empire, and his children, through fear. The question that drives the whole series is deceptively simple: when Logan finally steps aside, who gets the crown?

All of his children want it, and none of them is ready. Kendall, played by Jeremy Strong, is desperate to be taken seriously but crumbles the moment his father looks at him. Shiv, played by Sarah Snook, is clever and political, yet keeps underestimating how badly she craves Logan's approval. Roman, played by Kieran Culkin, hides behind an endless stream of filthy jokes. Then there is Connor, the eldest, who lives in his own comfortable bubble. Orbiting the family are two of the show's best creations: Tom, Shiv's eager, insecure husband, and Cousin Greg, a gangly outsider who arrives knowing nothing and learns, alarmingly fast, how to survive.

What makes Succession so addictive is that nobody ever says what they mean. A chat about lunch is really a negotiation; a compliment is often a threat. The camera behaves like a nosy guest, drifting around the room and suddenly zooming in on a face at exactly the wrong moment, so you feel as if you are eavesdropping on people who would never let you through the door.

And it is very, very funny. The insults are so inventive that fans collect them, and the humour is the uncomfortable kind: you laugh, then immediately wonder what that says about you. Critics often compare the show to King Lear, Shakespeare's tragedy about an old king who divides his kingdom between his children. It is not a lazy comparison. Underneath the private jets and boardroom battles, Succession asks something painfully human: can people who were never truly loved ever learn to trust anyone?

The industry agreed that it was special. The series won the Emmy for best drama three times, and its grand, slightly mocking theme music by Nicholas Britell took on a life of its own online.

A word of advice for newcomers: be patient. The Roys are hard to like in the first few episodes, and that is the point. Give it time, work out what each of them really wants, and you may find yourself caring deeply about people you would cross the street to avoid.

title: Better Call Saul: The Slow Fall of a Good Man
ru: Как приквел «Во все тяжкие» оказался не хуже оригинала и чем он цепляет
text:
Spin-offs are usually where good shows go to die. A popular character is pulled out of a hit series, given a story of their own, and quietly fades away within a couple of seasons. Better Call Saul, which ran on AMC from 2015 to 2022, did the opposite. Many fans now argue, with completely straight faces, that it is even better than the show it came from.

That show was Breaking Bad, and Better Call Saul is its prequel. Created by Vince Gilligan and Peter Gould, it tells how Jimmy McGill, a small-time lawyer with a big heart and a weakness for shortcuts, gradually turns into Saul Goodman, the flashy, morally flexible criminal lawyer that Breaking Bad fans already knew. Bob Odenkirk, previously best known for comedy, plays him with such warmth that you keep hoping he will make the right choice, even though you know, deep down, where the road ends.

That is the genius of the idea. There is no mystery about the destination; all the suspense lies in the journey. Why would a man who wanted so badly to be respectable give it all up? The answer is spread across six seasons and tied to the people around Jimmy. His older brother Chuck, played by Michael McKean, is a brilliant, proud lawyer who never quite believes Jimmy can change. Kim Wexler, played by Rhea Seehorn, is a sharp, ambitious colleague who understands Jimmy better than anyone, and she became many viewers' favourite character. Running alongside Jimmy's story is a darker one, following Mike Ehrmantraut, a quiet former police officer, as he drifts into the world of the drug cartels.

Better Call Saul is a slow show, and proud of it. It will happily spend several minutes watching someone carry out a small, practical task, and somehow make it gripping. The visuals are just as patient: wide shots of the New Mexico desert, carefully framed offices, colours that seem to shift with Jimmy's mood. Several seasons open with short black-and-white scenes set after the events of Breaking Bad, in which a nervous man calling himself Gene works at a cinnamon-roll shop in a shopping mall in Omaha. They are some of the most unsettling minutes in the whole series.

Here is a fun detail: the name Saul Goodman is a pun. Say it quickly and it sounds like “s'all good, man”, exactly the kind of reassuring line a slippery lawyer would love. And a more bitter one: despite dozens of Emmy nominations, the series never won a single award, something fans still bring up whenever they get the chance.

You do not need to have seen Breaking Bad to enjoy it, although you will catch more references if you have. Either way, this is a story about how good people go bad: not all at once, but one small compromise at a time.

title: True Detective Season One: Darkness in the Bayou
ru: Первый сезон «Настоящего детектива»: два детектива, Луизиана и история, рассказанная через два времени
text:
In 2014, two of Hollywood's most familiar faces walked into the Louisiana swamps and came out with one of the most talked-about seasons of television of the decade. The first season of True Detective, created for HBO by the novelist Nic Pizzolatto, is a crime story, but it is also a slow, haunting meditation on time, guilt and the stories people tell themselves in order to survive.

The plot follows two detectives, Rust Cohle and Marty Hart, played by Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson. In 1995, they are called to a bizarre murder: a young woman's body has been posed in a field with deer antlers on her head, surrounded by strange little sculptures made of sticks. Seventeen years later, in 2012, both men are interviewed separately by other detectives about that old case. The show cuts constantly between the two timelines, and you soon realise that what the men say in the interview room does not always match what we see in the past.

The heart of the season is the partnership itself. Marty is a family man who presents himself as solid and reliable, while being far less honest than he pretends. Rust is a loner with a bleak philosophy, who delivers long, gloomy speeches about human existence in the car while Marty begs him to stop talking. Their arguments are often darkly funny, and they turn what could have been a standard police procedural into a study of two very different kinds of damaged men. One of Rust's lines, that time is a flat circle, became an internet catchphrase almost overnight.

Unusually for television, all eight episodes were directed by one person, Cary Joji Fukunaga, which gives the season the feel of a single long film. His most famous achievement comes in the fourth episode: a continuous shot of about six minutes, with no visible cut, following Rust through a chaotic raid on a housing project. Fans still rewatch it, trying to work out how it was done.

The setting matters as much as the characters. The Louisiana of True Detective is a landscape of oil refineries, burned-out churches and endless flat fields under heavy grey skies. Even in daylight, it feels as if something terrible is hiding just out of sight. The writers also borrowed from old horror fiction, including a mysterious figure called the Yellow King, which sent curious viewers hunting for The King in Yellow, an 1895 collection of strange stories by Robert W. Chambers.

True Detective is an anthology series, which means each season tells a new story with a new cast, so you can watch the first one entirely on its own. It is dark, slow and occasionally very heavy. But if you like crime stories that stay with you for days after the credits roll, it is hard to beat.

title: BoJack Horseman: The Saddest Cartoon About a Horse
ru: Как мультсериал про говорящего коня-актёра оказался одним из самых честных шоу о взрослой жизни
text:
On the surface, BoJack Horseman sounds like a joke that got out of hand: a cartoon about a talking horse who once starred in a cheesy nineties sitcom. Look a little closer, though, and you find one of the most honest shows ever made about loneliness, fame and the slow, difficult work of becoming a better person.

The series was created by Raphael Bob-Waksberg, with distinctive character designs by the artist Lisa Hanawalt, and ran on Netflix for six seasons, from 2014 to 2020. Will Arnett voices BoJack, a former TV star whose career peaked decades ago with a family sitcom called Horsin' Around. Now he lives in a huge house in the hills above Los Angeles, drinks too much, insults everyone and spends a worrying amount of time watching reruns of his own show.

Around him is a memorable cast. Princess Carolyn, a pink cat, is his agent and on-and-off girlfriend, permanently juggling ten phone calls at once. Todd, voiced by Aaron Paul, is a cheerful slacker who once crashed on BoJack's couch and simply never left. Diane Nguyen, voiced by Alison Brie, is a thoughtful writer hired to ghost-write BoJack's memoir, which means writing the book for him under his name. And then there is Mr. Peanutbutter, a relentlessly happy Labrador and BoJack's old sitcom rival, who seems to succeed at everything without trying.

Their world, where humans and talking animals live side by side, is packed with visual jokes. Almost every background hides a pun or a sight gag, and fans love pausing the screen to hunt for them. In the first season, thanks to one of BoJack's worst ideas, the letter D disappears from the famous sign above the city, and from then on everyone in the show calls it Hollywoo.

What makes the series stand out is the way its tone slowly changes. The early episodes feel like a fairly standard adult comedy, but as the seasons go on, the writers dig into BoJack's childhood, his addictions and the damage he does to the people who care about him. The show refuses to offer easy redemption. It keeps asking whether saying sorry is ever enough, and its answer is complicated.

It is also surprisingly bold in its form. One celebrated episode in the third season, Fish Out of Water, takes place at an underwater film festival where BoJack cannot speak, so almost the whole episode plays out without dialogue. Another, in the fifth season, consists largely of a single long speech that BoJack gives at a funeral.

BoJack Horseman is not easy viewing, and it can hit hard if you have ever felt stuck in your own life. But it is also full of brilliant wordplay and silly slapstick, and it treats its audience like adults. Few cartoons can make you laugh at a horse pun and then quietly break your heart five minutes later.

title: Chernobyl: When a Mini-Series Tells the Truth About Lies
ru: Мини-сериал HBO о катастрофе 1986 года: почему он так впечатлил зрителей и что в нём художественный вымысел
text:
Most viewers knew how the story ended before the first episode began. In April 1986, a reactor exploded at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in Soviet Ukraine. Yet when HBO and Sky released the five-part mini-series Chernobyl in 2019, audiences around the world watched it with the tension usually reserved for thrillers. The question was never what happened. It was how it happened, and why so many people tried to pretend it hadn't.

The series was written by Craig Mazin, an American screenwriter whose earlier career had been mostly in comedy, including two of the Hangover sequels, and directed by Johan Renck. Jared Harris plays Valery Legasov, the scientist sent to help manage the disaster, and Stellan Skarsgård plays Boris Shcherbina, the senior official at his side. At first, the two men distrust each other completely. Over five episodes, they develop a grudging respect that becomes one of the most moving parts of the story.

What struck many viewers was the attention to detail. The flats, the cars, the uniforms and even the wallpaper look convincingly Soviet, and plenty of Russian-speaking viewers were surprised by how much the creators got right. Much of the filming took place in Lithuania, including at a closed power plant with reactors of the same type as Chernobyl's. The Icelandic composer Hildur Guðnadóttir built the eerie score partly from sounds she recorded inside that real plant, which is one reason the music feels less like music and more like a warning.

The show's true subject, however, is not radiation but lies. Again and again, officials hide information, play down the danger and punish people who tell the truth, because admitting failure is politically unthinkable. The series suggests that the real cost of lies is not only the immediate damage, but the way they slowly make the truth impossible to recognise.

It is worth remembering that Chernobyl is a drama, not a documentary. Some events are compressed or rearranged, and some characters were invented. The best-known example is Ulana Khomyuk, the determined physicist played by Emily Watson, who never existed; she represents the many scientists who helped investigate the accident. Mazin was open about these choices and discussed them in a companion podcast released alongside the series. Some historians also pointed out scenes that were exaggerated for dramatic effect.

Even so, the result is remarkable. Chernobyl won the Emmy for outstanding limited series, earned enormous praise from audiences, and sent many viewers off to read about the real history. It is not a comfortable watch: several scenes, especially those set in the hospital, are genuinely hard to sit through. But it is a powerful reminder that a disaster is never only technical. It is also about the people who decide, at every step, whether or not to tell the truth.

title: Severance: What If You Could Leave Work at Work?
ru: «Разделение»: жуткая и смешная сатира на офисную жизнь, где память о работе отделена от личной жизни
text:
Plenty of people dream of forgetting about work the moment they leave the office. Severance takes that wish and turns it into one of the strangest, funniest and most unsettling shows of recent years. Created by Dan Erickson, with many episodes directed by Ben Stiller, the series premiered on Apple TV+ in 2022 and returned for a long-awaited second season in 2025.

The idea is simple and chilling. At a secretive corporation called Lumon Industries, some employees agree to a surgical procedure called severance, which splits their memory in two. The person who exists at work, known as the innie, has no idea who they are outside the building. The outie, meanwhile, goes home every evening with no memory of what happened all day. And the two halves have no easy way to talk to each other.

Our guide to this world is Mark Scout, played by Adam Scott, who chose the procedure to escape a painful loss in his private life. At work, he leads a tiny team in a department called Macrodata Refinement. Their job is to stare at screens full of numbers and drag the ones that feel “scary” into digital bins. Nobody knows why. Nobody is supposed to ask. When a new colleague, Helly, played by Britt Lower, wakes up on a conference table with no idea who she is and immediately tries to quit, the team's carefully managed routine begins to crack.

Part of the fun is how precisely the show mocks office culture. Lumon rewards good performance with finger traps, erasers and, for the very best workers, a waffle party. Managers speak in cheerful corporate language that hides something much darker, and staff are expected to revere the company's founder, Kier Eagan, almost like a prophet. Anyone who has survived a pointless team-building session will laugh, and then shiver.

The look of the show adds to the unease. Lumon's offices are white, spotless and almost blindingly bright, with empty corridors that seem to go on forever. The computers are chunky and oddly old-fashioned, as if they came straight out of the eighties, so it is never quite clear when the story is set.

The supporting cast is superb. John Turturro and Christopher Walken play two older employees whose quiet friendship turns out to be surprisingly touching, Patricia Arquette is deeply unnerving as Mark's boss, and Tramell Tillman steals almost every scene as a smiling supervisor whose politeness feels like a threat.

Beneath the jokes, Severance asks serious questions. If your innie has feelings, friendships and hopes of its own, is it really you? And does the person who signed the contract have the right to decide its fate? Erickson has said the idea grew out of his own experience of dull office jobs, which may explain why the show feels so uncomfortably familiar.

The pace is slow and the mysteries are revealed piece by piece, so it rewards patience. But if you enjoy puzzles, dark humour and the occasional surreal dance party, it is time to clock in.

title: Mr. Robot: A Hacker Story That Gets Technology Right
ru: «Мистер Робот»: психологический триллер о хакере, где технологии показаны реалистично
text:
Hollywood has a long and embarrassing history of getting hacking wrong. On screen, hackers usually type furiously for ten seconds, a green progress bar fills up, and someone announces that they are in. Mr. Robot, which ran on USA Network from 2015 to 2019, was different. It became famous among programmers and security experts for something very few shows have managed: it got the technology right.

Created by Sam Esmail, the series follows Elliot Alderson, a young cybersecurity engineer in New York, played by Rami Malek in the role that made him a star. By day, Elliot protects companies from attacks at a firm called Allsafe. By night, he hacks the people around him, reading their emails and digging up their secrets, sometimes to protect others and sometimes simply because he can. He is painfully anxious and finds it almost impossible to connect with anyone. Then a mysterious man who calls himself Mr. Robot, played by Christian Slater, invites him to join an underground hacker group called fsociety. Their goal is to bring down E Corp, a giant conglomerate that Elliot always hears as Evil Corp, and wipe out the debts of ordinary people.

The technical side is unusually careful. The show worked with advisers who had real security experience, and the screens show genuine tools and commands instead of colourful nonsense. Many of the attacks rely on methods that real criminals use, especially social engineering, the art of tricking people into handing over passwords or access. Plenty of experts said it was the first time they had watched their profession on screen without cringing.

But Mr. Robot is not a technical manual. It is a psychological thriller, and Elliot is a deeply unreliable narrator. He speaks directly to the viewer, whom he treats as an imaginary friend, and he does not always tell us everything, or even know it himself. The camera often pushes characters into the bottom corner of the frame, leaving a large empty space above them, as if the world is pressing down on their heads.

Esmail took creative control seriously: from the second season on, he directed every episode himself. The show also rewards attentive viewers with small jokes. The episodes of the first season are titled like computer files, ending in extensions such as .mov or .mkv, while the final season names its episodes after error codes used on the web, including the famous 404, meaning “not found”. One episode of that last season contains almost no dialogue at all, yet it is one of the tensest hours of the whole series.

Malek won an Emmy for the role in 2016, and the show built a passionate following. It is dark, sometimes confusing, and it demands your full attention, which is exactly why its twists land so hard. If you have ever wondered what a hacker's life might really look like, minus the green progress bars, this is the place to start.

title: Rick and Morty: Chaos, Science and Surprising Depth
ru: Почему безумный мультсериал о гениальном учёном и его внуке так популярен и что скрывается за шутками
text:
Rick and Morty began life as a rude, cheap parody. In the mid-2000s, Justin Roiland made a crude short cartoon mocking the famous time-travelling duo from Back to the Future for a monthly short-film festival. A few years later, he and Dan Harmon, the creator of the cult sitcom Community, developed the idea into a series for Adult Swim. It premiered in 2013 and grew into one of the most popular animated shows of its era.

The setup is easy to describe. Rick Sanchez is a cynical, hard-drinking scientist who may well be the smartest being in the universe. He moves in with his daughter Beth's family and drags his anxious, kind-hearted grandson Morty on adventures across space, time and countless parallel dimensions, thanks to a portal gun that can open a door to almost anywhere. Back at home, Beth, her insecure husband Jerry and their teenage daughter Summer deal with the consequences, which are frequently disastrous.

On the surface, the show is pure chaos. A typical episode might feature a planet-sized monster, a talking household gadget and a flood of gross-out jokes. Two fan-favourite episodes are built around Rick flicking through channels on a cable box that picks up TV from other dimensions, showing one absurd programme after another; much of that material was famously improvised. In another, Rick turns himself into a pickle simply to avoid a family therapy session, and somehow ends up fighting his way through a sewer full of rats.

But fans keep coming back for what hides beneath the jokes. Because Rick can visit an infinite number of realities, the show keeps poking at a terrifying idea: if there are endless versions of you, does anything you do actually matter? Rick's answer usually seems to be no, yet the series keeps showing how much that attitude costs him and the people who love him. Some episodes end on a note of real sadness, and the show is often at its best when a ridiculous premise suddenly turns serious.

Rick and Morty also shows how wild fan culture can get. In 2017, an episode mentioned a dipping sauce that McDonald's had sold for a short time back in 1998 to promote a Disney film. Fans demanded it so loudly that the company brought it back for a single day, and some restaurants were overwhelmed by crowds who could not get any. It was a vivid reminder of how passionate, and occasionally unreasonable, a fandom can be.

The show is not for everyone. Its humour can be crude, and Rick is often cruel. But underneath the slime and the explosions, it is a surprisingly thoughtful series about family, intelligence and the loneliness of being the smartest person in every room, or in every universe.

title: Cyberpunk 2077: From Disaster to Redemption
ru: История провального запуска Cyberpunk 2077 и того, как студия постепенно вернула доверие игроков
text:
Few video games have been as hyped as Cyberpunk 2077, and few launches have gone as badly. Yet the story of this game did not end in December 2020. It became something much rarer: a comeback.

The game was developed by CD Projekt Red, the Polish studio behind The Witcher 3, one of the most admired role-playing games of the previous decade. It is based on Cyberpunk, a tabletop role-playing game created by Mike Pondsmith in the late 1980s, and it is set in Night City, a vast neon-lit metropolis on the west coast of America, ruled by mega-corporations and street gangs. You play as V, a mercenary trying to make a name for themselves in the criminal underworld. After a job goes horribly wrong, V ends up with an experimental chip in their head, and on that chip lives the digital ghost of Johnny Silverhand, a rebellious rock star who died decades earlier. Johnny is played by Keanu Reeves, whose surprise appearance at the E3 trade show in 2019, when he answered a shouting fan with “You're breathtaking!”, instantly became a meme.

Expectations were enormous, and the release was delayed several times. When the game finally arrived, players on powerful PCs found an ambitious, if buggy, adventure. Players on the older PlayStation 4 and Xbox One, however, often found something close to unplayable: low frame rates, blurry textures, characters falling through floors and cars appearing out of thin air. The backlash was immediate. Sony took the unusual step of removing the game from the PlayStation Store and offering refunds, and the studio publicly apologised.

What happened next is the interesting part. Instead of abandoning the project, CD Projekt Red spent years fixing it. Patch after patch improved performance and stability, and in 2023 a major update reworked the skill system, the police and much of the combat. The same year brought Phantom Liberty, a spy-thriller expansion starring Idris Elba, which many critics called some of the best content in the entire game.

Help also came from an unexpected direction. In 2022, Netflix released Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, an anime series set in Night City and made by the Japanese studio Trigger. It was a hit, and many viewers who fell in love with it went back to the game, discovering a far better version than the one that had disappointed everyone at launch. The number of people playing rose sharply again.

Today, Cyberpunk 2077 is often held up, alongside No Man's Sky, as one of the great redemption stories in gaming. It is also a lesson about the danger of releasing a game before it is ready, and about how valuable it is when a studio chooses to fix its mistakes instead of moving on.

The city itself remains the real star: rain-soaked streets, giant holographic advertisements and a constant buzz of danger. If you gave up on it in 2020, it might be time for a second look.
