title: A Letter from a School of Magic
about: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (2001)
wiki: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (film)
ru: Первый фильм о Гарри Поттере: мальчик узнаёт, что он волшебник
text:
Harry Potter sleeps in a tiny cupboard under the stairs. His aunt and uncle, the Dursleys, are cold and unkind to him, and his spoiled cousin Dudley gets everything he wants. Then one day a letter arrives for Harry. His uncle takes it away. The next day more letters come. Soon hundreds of them are flying into the house through the fireplace.

This is the start of Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, the first film about the famous boy wizard. It came out in 2001. Chris Columbus directed it, and it was based on the first book by J.K. Rowling. In America the film has a different name: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone.

The letters come from Hogwarts, a school of magic in an old castle. A giant of a man called Hagrid finds Harry and tells him the big news: Harry is a wizard, and his parents were a witch and a wizard too.

At Hogwarts Harry makes two best friends: funny, nervous Ron Weasley and very clever Hermione Granger. The castle is full of surprises. The stairs move, the people in the paintings talk, and an old magic hat tells each new student which house they will join. Harry also tries Quidditch, a sport on flying broomsticks, and he is brilliant at it from the very first day.

But something dark is hiding in the school, and the three friends decide to find out what it is.

Daniel Radcliffe was only eleven when he got the role of Harry. He, Rupert Grint and Emma Watson played the three friends in all eight films, so fans watched them grow up on screen.

title: A Simple Man in a Big History
ru: Добрый и простой человек случайно оказывается в центре американской истории
text:
A man sits on a bench at a bus stop with a box of chocolates. He starts talking to the stranger next to him, and soon he is telling the story of his whole life. And what a life it is!

That man is Forrest Gump. Tom Hanks played him in the 1994 film by Robert Zemeckis, which was based on a novel by Winston Groom. Forrest is not very smart, but he is kind, honest and always does his best.

As a boy he has to wear metal braces on his legs, and other kids are cruel to him. One day they chase him on their bikes, and as he runs, the braces break apart. Forrest is free, and he is incredibly fast. After that, running changes his life again and again.

Forrest never plans anything, but he keeps ending up in the middle of American history. He plays college football, fights in the Vietnam War, becomes a ping-pong star and plays in China and starts a shrimp business. Shrimp are small sea animals that people love to eat. Once he simply starts running and doesn't stop for more than three years. Through all of it, he never forgets Jenny, his best friend from childhood and the only girl he loves.

The film is famous for its special effects. Forrest meets real American presidents, because the filmmakers put Tom Hanks into old TV news. It still looks real today.

Forrest Gump won six Oscars, including Best Picture and Best Actor for Hanks. There is even a real restaurant chain named after Forrest's shrimp company: Bubba Gump.

title: A Farm Boy Among the Stars
ru: Первые «Звёздные войны»: фильм, который изменил кино
text:
In 1977, almost nobody expected much from a strange space film with robots, laser swords and a big hairy co-pilot. A few months later, people were standing in long lines outside cinemas to watch it again and again.

George Lucas wrote and directed Star Wars. The story begins on Tatooine, a desert planet with two suns. Luke Skywalker is a young farm boy who dreams of adventure. Everything changes when his uncle buys two robots: golden, worried C-3PO and small, brave R2-D2. Inside R2-D2 there is a secret message from Princess Leia. She is fighting against the evil Empire, and she needs help fast.

Soon Luke meets old Obi-Wan Kenobi, who tells him about the Jedi knights and the Force, a mysterious energy that connects all living things. They also find a pilot: Han Solo, who cares more about money than about saving anyone, and his friend Chewbacca, a tall Wookiee covered in fur. Their enemy is Darth Vader, a dark figure in black armor. His heavy breathing is one of the most famous sounds in cinema.

The film looked like nothing before it. Lucas started his own effects company, Industrial Light & Magic, to make the space battles, and John Williams wrote the music. Today you probably know the main theme even without seeing the film.

Star Wars became the highest-earning film in history at that time. Later it got a longer name, Episode IV: A New Hope, and it started one of the biggest stories in pop culture.

title: What If the World Is Not Real?
ru: Хакер узнаёт, что привычный мир — компьютерная симуляция
text:
Have you ever had a dream that felt completely real? Now imagine that your whole life is that dream, and you have never woken up. This is the frightening idea behind The Matrix, the science fiction film that changed action cinema in 1999.

The film was written and directed by the Wachowskis. Keanu Reeves plays Thomas Anderson, a quiet programmer at a software company by day and a hacker called Neo by night. He feels that something is wrong with the world, but he cannot say what. Then a mysterious woman, Trinity, leads him to Morpheus, a calm and powerful man who offers him a choice. If Neo takes a blue pill, he will wake up in his bed and go back to his normal life. If he takes a red pill, he will learn the truth. Today, “taking the red pill” is a common English expression for discovering an uncomfortable truth.

The truth is that Neo's world is a computer simulation, called the Matrix, and humanity is trapped inside it. Inside the program, the rules can be bent, and people who understand this can jump between buildings or dodge bullets. The program's guards, the Agents in dark suits and sunglasses, are led by the cold and unforgettable Agent Smith, played by Hugo Weaving.

The film's action looked like nothing audiences had seen before. The actors trained in martial arts for months with the Hong Kong choreographer Yuen Woo-ping. The famous “bullet time” effect, in which time almost stops while the camera seems to fly around a character, was created with a long line of cameras that photographed the actor from many angles at once. Soon, everyone was copying it. The Matrix won four Oscars, including one for visual effects.

Here is a fun fact: the designer of the famous green computer code that falls down the screen has said that the symbols came from Japanese cookbooks belonging to his wife. So the code of the Matrix is, in a way, a collection of sushi recipes.

And another: Will Smith has said that he was offered the role of Neo but turned it down.

The Matrix was followed by two sequels in 2003 and a fourth film in 2021. But the first one is still the best place to start, and its main question is still worth asking: how do you know that your world is real?

o: A choice between a blue pill and a red pill

title: A Small Hobbit and a Very Big Task
about: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring (2001)
wiki: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
ru: Первый фильм трилогии «Властелин колец» и как его снимали в Новой Зеландии
text:
Hobbits are small, peaceful people who love good food, comfortable homes and not having adventures. So when a powerful evil ring falls into the hands of a young hobbit called Frodo Baggins, it seems like the worst possible choice of hero. That is exactly the point of The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring.

The film, released in 2001, is the first part of Peter Jackson's adaptation of J. R. R. Tolkien's famous novel. Frodo inherits the Ring from his uncle Bilbo, and the wizard Gandalf discovers that it belongs to the Dark Lord Sauron, who wants it back. The only way to destroy it is to throw it into the fire of Mount Doom, deep in Sauron's land of Mordor. Frodo sets off with his loyal friend Sam, and later they become part of a group of nine companions: four hobbits, two men, an elf, a dwarf and a wizard. This group is the Fellowship.

The way the film was made is an adventure in itself. Peter Jackson, a director from New Zealand, convinced the studio to let him film all three parts of the story at the same time. Filming lasted more than a year, all around New Zealand, whose mountains, rivers and green hills became Middle-earth. The village of Hobbiton was built on a farm near the town of Matamata, and today it is a popular tourist attraction where you can visit the little round doors of the hobbit houses.

Making hobbits look small next to tall humans was a real challenge. The filmmakers used special camera tricks, such as forced perspective: actors sat at different distances from the camera so that one looked much smaller than the other, even though they seemed to be side by side. Sometimes small body doubles or extra-large copies of furniture were used.

The cast included Elijah Wood as Frodo, Ian McKellen as Gandalf and Viggo Mortensen as Aragorn. Christopher Lee, who played the wizard Saruman, was the only member of the cast who had actually met Tolkien.

The film won four Oscars, and the trilogy ended in triumph: the third film, The Return of the King, won eleven, including Best Picture. Not bad for a story about a small person who just wanted to stay at home.

o: Gandalf must break it with his staff
It must be thrown into the fire of Mount Doom

title: Stealing Ideas from Dreams
ru: Фильм Кристофера Нолана о ворах, которые проникают в чужие сны
text:
Most thieves break into houses. Dom Cobb breaks into minds. In Christopher Nolan's film Inception (2010), Cobb, played by Leonardo DiCaprio, is an expert in “extraction”: he enters people's dreams and steals secrets that they would never tell anyone while awake.

Then a powerful businessman, Saito, offers him a job that seems impossible. Instead of stealing an idea, Cobb must plant one, so deeply that the victim believes it is his own. This is called inception. The target is Robert Fischer, the young heir to a huge company, who will soon control his dying father's business. The reward for Cobb is something he wants more than money: the chance to go home to his children.

Like every good heist film, Inception lets us watch a team being put together. There is Arthur, Cobb's calm and careful partner; Eames, a charming forger who can take the appearance of other people inside dreams; Yusuf, a chemist who makes the sleeping drugs; and Ariadne, a young architecture student who designs the dream worlds. Through her questions, the audience learns the rules.

And the rules are clever. Inside a dream you can have another dream, and then another, like boxes inside boxes. Time moves slower at each level, so a few minutes in the real world can become hours or even years deeper down. To wake someone up, you give them a “kick”, a feeling of falling. And because it is easy to forget which world you are in, each dreamer carries a “totem”, a small personal object that behaves differently in dreams. Cobb's totem is a little spinning top.

Many of the film's most amazing scenes were made for real, not only with computers. For a famous fight in a hotel corridor, the team built a huge corridor that could rotate, so the actor Joseph Gordon-Levitt really had to fight while the walls and ceiling turned around him.

Hans Zimmer's music is just as famous. Its deep, heavy horn sound was copied in countless trailers. Zimmer has explained that parts of the score come from an old French song by Édith Piaf, slowed down, and that song also plays an important role in the story.

Inception won four Oscars, and its final shot still makes people argue. Watch it, and then decide for yourself what you saw.

o: Stealing a secret from someone's dream
Planting an idea so the person thinks it is their own
Waking someone up with a feeling of falling

o: She pretends to be other people

title: Hope Behind Prison Walls
ru: Фильм, который провалился в кинотеатрах, а потом стал всеобщим любимцем
text:
In 1994, a prison drama with a strange name arrived in American cinemas, and few people went to see it. A few years later, it had become one of the most loved films ever made. This is the story of The Shawshank Redemption.

The film is based on a short novel by Stephen King, the master of horror, although there are no monsters in it. It was written and directed by Frank Darabont. In 1947, a quiet banker called Andy Dufresne, played by Tim Robbins, is sent to Shawshank prison for life. He has been found guilty of murdering his wife and her lover. He says he is innocent, but nobody listens.

At first, Andy seems too calm and too soft for such a brutal place. The story is told by Red, played by Morgan Freeman, an older prisoner who is known as the man who can get things: cigarettes, chocolate, magazines, almost anything. Slowly, the two men become friends. Red has spent so long in prison that he has almost forgotten how to hope. Andy, on the other hand, refuses to give up. He uses his skills as a banker to help the guards with their taxes, fights for years to build a prison library, and once even plays opera music to the whole prison through the loudspeakers. For a few minutes, every prisoner stops and listens.

That is what the film is really about: not escape, not crime, but hope, and how dangerous and necessary it can be in a place designed to kill it. Morgan Freeman's warm, slow narration is one of the reasons people return to the film again and again.

So why did it fail at first? The title was confusing, prison films were not fashionable, and it had to compete with huge hits of the same year, such as Forrest Gump and Pulp Fiction. It was nominated for seven Oscars, but it won none. Then it was released on video and shown on television, and something unusual happened. People told their friends about it. They watched it again. Its audience kept growing, and for many years it has been at or near the top of IMDb's list of the best films of all time, chosen by ordinary viewers.

Many of the prison scenes were shot in an old prison in Mansfield, Ohio. Today, fans travel there to walk through the same corridors as Andy and Red.

o: He stole money from his bank
He was found guilty of murdering his wife and her lover

title: The Godfather: A Family Business Like No Other
ru: Почему «Крёстный отец» Копполы до сих пор считается одним из величайших фильмов
text:
The Godfather opens not with a gunshot but with a wedding. Outside, in the summer sun, guests dance, eat and sing. Inside, in a dark office with the blinds closed, a quiet old man listens to people asking for favors — favors that will have to be repaid one day. In those first minutes, Francis Ford Coppola's 1972 film tells you almost everything about the Corleone family: love and violence live in the same house.

Based on Mario Puzo's bestselling novel, the film follows the Corleones, one of the most powerful Mafia families in New York after the Second World War. Marlon Brando plays the head of the family, Vito Corleone, with a soft, raspy voice and the calm of a man who never needs to shout. James Caan is his hot-tempered eldest son, Sonny, and Robert Duvall plays Tom Hagen, the family's adopted son and lawyer. But the heart of the story is Michael, the youngest son, played by Al Pacino. When we first meet him, he is a war hero in uniform who tells his girlfriend, Kay, that he wants nothing to do with the family business.

The film is the story of how that changes, and it is fascinating precisely because the change happens slowly. Pacino's performance lives in small things: the way he listens, the way his face grows harder and stiller with every scene. By the end, you may feel you have watched not a gangster movie but a tragedy.

It almost did not turn out this way. Paramount, the studio, had doubts about nearly everything. Executives did not want Brando, who had a reputation for being difficult, and they thought Pacino, then little known, was too short and too unfamiliar for the part. Coppola fought for both, and both performances are now considered among the greatest in film history.

Visually, The Godfather is famous for its darkness. Cinematographer Gordon Willis often lit scenes from above, leaving the characters' eyes in shadow, so it is hard to tell what they are thinking. Nino Rota's sad, waltz-like main theme turned the story into something close to opera. Coppola also filled the film with family rituals — weddings, christenings, Sunday dinners — so that its violence always erupts in the middle of ordinary life.

The film won the Academy Award for Best Picture, and Brando won Best Actor, although he refused to accept the award in protest at Hollywood's treatment of Native Americans. The sequel, The Godfather Part II (1974), also won Best Picture, and many people argue that it is even better.

More than fifty years later, the film's influence is everywhere, from The Sopranos to endless jokes about offers nobody can turn down. Yet what keeps people coming back is not the shootouts. It is the question at the center of the story: how far would you go for your family, and what would be left of you afterwards?

title: Parasite: Upstairs, Downstairs
ru: Южнокорейский фильм, который первым из неанглоязычных получил «Оскар» за лучший фильм
text:
In February 2020, something happened that Hollywood had never seen before. A Korean-language film about two families won the Academy Award for Best Picture. Parasite, directed by Bong Joon-ho, became the first film not in English ever to take the top prize, and it also collected Best Director, Best Original Screenplay and Best International Feature Film on the same night. Months earlier, it had won the Palme d'Or, the top award at the Cannes Film Festival.

The story begins almost underground. The Kim family lives in a cramped semi-basement apartment in Seoul, where the windows are at street level and drunk men sometimes relieve themselves right outside. The father, Ki-taek, played by Song Kang-ho, is cheerful and unemployed. His wife and two grown-up children are smart, quick and equally broke. They fold pizza boxes for cash and steal Wi-Fi from the neighbors by holding their phones up near the bathroom ceiling.

Then the son gets a chance to work as an English tutor for the teenage daughter of the wealthy Park family, who live in a beautiful modern house on a hill. One by one, the Kims find clever and not entirely honest ways to get the rest of the family hired by the Parks. The first part of the film plays almost like a heist comedy, and it is very funny.

It would be a crime to say more about the plot, because Parasite changes direction more than once, and its surprises are a big part of the experience. What can be said is that Bong builds the whole film around height. The rich live up the hill, surrounded by light and space; the poor live down below, in darkness and damp. Characters are constantly climbing stairs or walking down them, and the camera never lets you forget who is above whom.

Another clever idea is smell. The Parks are polite, even kind in their careless way, but they keep noticing something about the Kims that cannot be washed away: a smell that marks them as people from a different world. It is a tiny detail that says a great deal about class, and it becomes more painful as the film goes on.

One of the most surprising facts about Parasite is that the Parks' stunning house does not exist. It was built as a set, carefully designed so that the camera could follow the characters through it and so that every window and staircase served the story.

The film looks at the gap between rich and poor without dividing the world neatly into heroes and villains, and that is perhaps why it connected with audiences in so many countries. Nobody in Parasite is purely good or purely evil. Everyone simply wants a better place in the house — and there is only so much room upstairs.

title: Casablanca: An Old Film That Still Works
ru: Чёрно-белая классика 1942 года: почему её до сих пор смотрят
text:
Casablanca should have been forgotten. It was one of dozens of films Warner Bros. made in 1942, a wartime romance shot quickly from a script that was still being rewritten while the cameras rolled. More than eighty years later, it still appears on almost every list of the greatest films ever made. So what is its secret?

The setting helps. During the Second World War, Casablanca, in French Morocco, was a waiting room for refugees trying to escape Nazi-occupied Europe. Many hoped to get exit visas to neutral Lisbon and from there to America. People sold their jewelry, their cars and sometimes their principles for the right piece of paper. In the middle of it all stands Rick's Café Américain, a nightclub where everyone turns up sooner or later.

Its owner, Rick Blaine, played by Humphrey Bogart, is a bitter American who insists that he takes risks for nobody. He drinks alone, plays chess against himself and refuses to take sides. Then one night Ilsa Lund, played by Ingrid Bergman, walks into his club with her husband, Victor Laszlo, a famous resistance leader on the run. Rick and Ilsa were once in love in Paris, and she left him without explanation. Now she needs his help.

What follows is a love triangle, a thriller and a political drama all at once. Bogart's tough, tired face is perfect for a man pretending not to care, and Bergman glows with the confusion of someone torn between two good choices. Claude Rains almost steals the film as Captain Renault, a charming, corrupt French police officer who changes his loyalties as easily as his hat.

Famously, the production was chaotic. The script was being finished during shooting, and the actors were reportedly unsure how the story would end. Instead of ruining the film, that uncertainty may have helped it: Bergman's Ilsa genuinely does not seem to know which man she will choose.

The film also carries a surprising emotional weight because of who was in it. Many of the actors were themselves refugees from Europe. In one famous scene, the customers at Rick's stand up and drown out a group of German officers by singing the French national anthem, and some of the tears on screen were reportedly real.

Casablanca gave the world several famous lines, but its most quoted one does not actually exist. Nobody in the film says “Play it again, Sam.” Ilsa does ask the pianist, Sam, to play their old song, “As Time Goes By”, but in different words. The misquote became so popular that Woody Allen later used it as the title of a play.

The film won the Academy Award for Best Picture, but its real victory is its survival. Black-and-white, slow by modern standards and made in a hurry, it still works because its characters face a question that never goes out of date: when the world is on fire, is your own happiness worth more than doing the right thing?

title: A Big House and Many People

text:
It is 1912. A rich English family lives in a huge house in the country. Upstairs, they wear beautiful clothes and eat dinner with many forks and knives. Downstairs, many servants cook, clean and carry everything. Downton Abbey shows both worlds.

The series is British. Julian Fellowes created it, and it ran from 2010 to 2015. It starts with real news: the Titanic sinks. The heir of the family — the man who gets the house and the money after the father — was on that ship. So who gets Downton now?

Upstairs lives the Crawley family: Robert, his American wife Cora and their three very different daughters, Mary, Edith and Sybil. Downstairs we meet Mr Carson, the serious butler, the kind Mrs Hughes, and many young maids and footmen. They have secrets, love stories and fights too.

For many fans, the best character is Violet, Robert's old mother. Maggie Smith plays her. Violet says terrible things in a very elegant way. Once a young man talks about the weekend, and she asks, “What is a weekend?” She never works, so for her every day is the same.

The house is real. It is Highclere Castle in the south of England, and you can visit it. After the series, there were films about the family too.

title: An American Girl in Paris

text:
Emily Cooper is young, smart and full of energy. She works in marketing in Chicago. One day her company needs someone in Paris, and Emily says yes. There is only one problem: she doesn't speak French.

Emily in Paris is an American series from Netflix. It started in 2020. Darren Star created it — he also made Sex and the City. Lily Collins plays Emily.

In Paris, Emily works at a small marketing company, Savoir. Her new colleagues are not happy. They think she is too loud, too fast and too American. Her boss, Sylvie, is elegant, cool and very cold to her. Emily smiles and works harder.

Emily posts photos of Paris on Instagram: croissants, flowers, old streets. Soon thousands of people follow her account, and this helps her at work. She finds friends too: Mindy, a funny girl from China who loves to sing, and Gabriel, a handsome chef who lives downstairs.

Many French critics laughed at the show. Real Paris, they said, is not so clean and pink. But millions of people around the world watch it — and then dream about a trip to Paris.

title: The Sopranos: The Show That Started a Golden Age
ru: Сериал о мафиозном боссе у психотерапевта, который изменил телевидение
text:
In the first episode of The Sopranos, a powerful New Jersey mob boss walks into a psychiatrist's office because he has started having panic attacks. He has no idea why. All he knows is that he collapsed at a family barbecue, and that he has become strangely attached to a family of wild ducks living in his swimming pool. When the ducks fly away, he feels lost.

That man is Tony Soprano, and over six seasons on HBO, from 1999 to 2007, he changed what television could be.

Created by David Chase, The Sopranos had a simple but brilliant idea: what if a gangster had the same problems as everyone else? Tony, played by James Gandolfini, worries about his teenage children, argues with his wife, Carmela, and struggles with his mother, Livia, who may be the most frightening character in the whole show. He just also happens to run a criminal organization, and some of his solutions involve violence.

Gandolfini's performance is the heart of the series. He makes Tony funny, charming, self-pitying and genuinely terrifying, sometimes within a single scene. You find yourself liking him, then feeling guilty for liking him, then being shocked all over again by what he does. Opposite him, Lorraine Bracco plays his therapist, Dr. Jennifer Melfi, whose sessions give the show its structure and give viewers a rare look inside a criminal's head.

Before The Sopranos, most American TV dramas were built for easy viewing. Each episode solved a problem, and the main characters were clearly good people. The Sopranos ignored those rules. It took its time, ended episodes without neat answers, played with dreams and symbols, and asked viewers to spend years with a man who never really changed for the better. Because HBO was a subscription channel without advertisers, Chase had a freedom that network writers could only dream of.

The result was a huge critical and commercial success. In 2004 it became the first cable series to win the Emmy for Outstanding Drama Series. More importantly, it showed TV executives that audiences would follow difficult, morally complicated main characters. Without Tony Soprano, it is hard to imagine Don Draper in Mad Men — a show created by Matthew Weiner, who had been a writer on The Sopranos — or Walter White in Breaking Bad. Many critics date the start of television's so-called Golden Age to that first visit to Dr. Melfi's office.

The show's final scene is still argued about by fans almost twenty years after it was broadcast. Without giving anything away, it is fair to say that it refused, one last time, to hand viewers the easy answers they wanted.

Gandolfini died in 2013, but Tony remains one of the great characters in any medium: a man who sits in a therapist's office and talks, at length and with real feeling, about everything except the one thing that might save him.

title: Mad Men: Selling Dreams in the 1960s
ru: Стильная драма о рекламном агентстве в Нью-Йорке 1960-х
text:
In 1960s New York, the men who worked in advertising on Madison Avenue were said to call themselves “mad men”. They wore sharp suits, drank whiskey before lunch, smoked in every meeting and sold Americans a dream of the perfect life — new cars, new kitchens, new cigarettes. Mad Men, which ran on AMC from 2007 to 2015, invites us into their offices and shows us how much was hiding behind the dream.

The series, created by Matthew Weiner, follows the staff of Sterling Cooper, a fictional advertising agency. At its center is Don Draper, the agency's brilliant creative director, played by Jon Hamm. Don is handsome, confident and almost frighteningly good at his job. He can stand in front of a client and, in two minutes, turn a product into a story about love, family or belonging. But his private life is a tangle of secrets, and the more we learn about him, the less sure we are of who he really is.

Around him is one of the finest ensemble casts on television. Peggy Olson, played by Elisabeth Moss, arrives as a shy young secretary and slowly fights her way into the male world of copywriters. Joan Holloway, played by Christina Hendricks, runs the office with absolute authority, even though the men around her rarely give her credit. Roger Sterling, the witty, lazy son of one of the agency's founders, gets many of the show's funniest lines.

Part of the pleasure of Mad Men is its period detail. The costumes, furniture and hairstyles are recreated so carefully that almost any frame could pass for a photograph from the time. Characters smoke constantly, drink at their desks and treat women in ways that make modern viewers wince. The show never preaches, but simply by showing how things were, it reveals how much has changed — and, sometimes, how little.

The show is also about advertising itself. Many episodes revolve around a pitch, the moment when Don presents an idea to a client. In one famous scene from the first season, he presents a slide projector not as a machine but as a time machine for memories, and the room falls silent. It is a beautiful speech, and also a slightly frightening one, because it shows how easily feelings can be turned into sales.

The world outside the agency is changing fast. Over seven seasons, the series moves through the decade, and real events, from the Kennedy assassination to the Moon landing, reach the characters through radios and television sets. Some of them adapt to the new times; others are left behind.

Mad Men was never a huge ratings hit, but critics adored it. It won the Emmy for Outstanding Drama Series four years in a row and helped establish AMC, alongside Breaking Bad, as a home for serious drama. Like Don's best pitches, it sells you something irresistible: style, wit and nostalgia. Then, quietly, it shows you the price.

title: Subtitles: Your Secret Teacher
about: How subtitles help you learn a language
ru: Как правильно пользоваться субтитрами, чтобы учить язык по сериалам
text:
You have probably heard this advice: “Watch series in English and you will learn the language.” It is true, but only if you do it the right way. If you watch with subtitles in your own language, your eyes read and your brain relaxes, and the English sound becomes just background music. Subtitles can be a great teacher, but you have to use them cleverly.

Fans have known the power of subtitles for a long time. In the 1980s and 1990s, many anime series were never released outside Japan, so fans translated them and added their own subtitles. These “fansubs” were copied and shared, first on video tapes and later on the internet. Many people who grew up with them say that this is how they first got used to listening to a foreign language.

So how do you use subtitles to learn? A good plan has three steps.

Step one: English audio with subtitles in your own language. This is fine at the beginning, especially with a series you already love. Try to notice a few phrases that you hear often, such as “What's going on?” or “I'll be right back.”

Step two: English audio with English subtitles. This is the most useful stage for most learners. You hear the words and see how they are written at the same time, so fast speech becomes easier to separate into words. If you don't understand a sentence, pause, read it again and listen again. It is slow, but it works.

Step three: no subtitles at all. Start with something easy and familiar, such as an episode you have already seen. You will not understand everything, and that is normal. Even native speakers sometimes turn on subtitles when actors whisper or speak with strong accents.

A few more tips. Choose shows with a lot of everyday conversation, like comedies or dramas about ordinary people, rather than fantasy films full of invented words. Short episodes are better than long films, because you can watch them more often. And don't stop to look up every word: write down only the phrases that you hear again and again.

If you follow this plan for a few months, something magical happens. One evening, you will realise that you have just watched a whole scene without reading anything.

title: Two Minutes to Sell a Film
ru: Кто и как делает трейлеры к фильмам и почему в них бывают сцены, которых нет в кино
text:
Two minutes. That is about how long a trailer has to make you want to see a film that took years and millions of dollars to make. No pressure.

Here is the first surprise: the word “trailer” comes from the fact that, in the early days of cinema, these short adverts were often shown after the main film. They trailed behind it, like a little boat behind a ship. Audiences preferred to leave when the film ended, so the adverts soon moved to the beginning, but the name stayed.

Most trailers are not made by the director of the film. They are created by specialised companies called trailer houses, whose editors watch the film and choose a few dozen tiny moments. Their job is to tell a story without telling the story: show the hero, the danger and the emotion, but hide the ending. Music does a huge part of the work, and there are composers who write only trailer music, full of drums, rising tension and sudden silence.

Studios usually release a short teaser first, often months before the premiere, just to make people curious. The full trailer comes later and shows more. Many fans complain that modern trailers show too much.

Have you ever noticed a scene in a trailer that is not in the film? There are several reasons for this. Trailers are often made while the film is still being edited, so some scenes are cut later. Sometimes special shots are filmed only for the trailer. A famous example is the first teaser for the 2002 film Spider-Man. It showed a helicopter caught in a giant web between the towers of the World Trade Center. After the attacks of 11 September 2001, the teaser was removed, and the scene never appeared in the film.

Missing scenes can even end up in court. In the United States, two fans sued a studio because an actress they had seen in a trailer did not appear in the film at all. A judge decided that a trailer is a kind of advertisement, which, like any advert, must not mislead people, so the case could go ahead.

And then there is the voice. For decades, many American trailers began with a deep, dramatic voice saying the same three words: “In a world...” The man behind that voice, Don LaFontaine, recorded thousands of trailers and became a legend of the industry.

title: Why British and American Series Sound Different
about: British vs American TV series: accents, vocabulary, format
ru: Почему британские и американские сериалы звучат по-разному — и дело не только в акценте
text:
Switch from an American sitcom to a British one, and the difference hits you within seconds. It is not only the accents. The jokes land differently, there are far fewer episodes, and even the word for a group of episodes is not the same.

Start with that word. Americans talk about seasons; the British usually call them series. So when a Brit mentions “the second series of Sherlock”, an American would say “season two”. It is a small difference, but it points to a bigger one: how many episodes there are.

A traditional American network show might run for twenty-two episodes a year, created by a large team of writers who sit together in a writers' room and shape stories almost like a production line. Many British shows, by contrast, have six episodes or fewer per series, and some are written by just one or two people. Sherlock had only three episodes per series, although each was about ninety minutes long. Fawlty Towers, one of the best-loved British comedies ever, made just twelve episodes in total.

The Office is the perfect example. The original British version, created by Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant, ran for two short series and two Christmas specials — fourteen episodes. The American remake ran for nine seasons and around two hundred episodes. Both are excellent, but they feel very different. The British boss, David Brent, is painfully awkward and often simply sad. His American equivalent, Michael Scott, gradually becomes someone the audience genuinely loves. British comedy is often comfortable letting failure stay failure; American comedy tends to look for warmth.

Then there is the language. Characters in British shows live in flats rather than apartments, queue instead of standing in line, and call each other “mate”. Something bad is “rubbish”, and “cheers” can mean thanks, goodbye or both. Learners also notice how much regional accents matter. In Peaky Blinders, set in Birmingham after the First World War, the characters' accent is part of who they are. American TV has regional accents too, but the leads of major shows more often speak a fairly neutral General American.

Production plays a role as well. Many British dramas and entertainment shows are made at studios near London, such as Elstree Studios, which has hosted everything from TV game shows to parts of the original Star Wars. Budgets are usually smaller than in the US, so British TV often relies on dialogue and performances rather than spectacle.

None of this makes one tradition better than the other. American TV is brilliant at long, addictive stories and characters you can live with for a decade. British TV is brilliant at short, sharp shows that end before they outstay their welcome. For a learner of English, the best strategy is simple: watch both. Your ears will thank you — or, as a British character might put it, cheers for that.

title: A Big Friend in the Forest
ru: Две сестры переезжают в деревню и встречают лесного духа Тоторо.
text:
Two sisters move to an old house in the Japanese countryside with their father. Satsuki is about ten. Mei is four, and she is not afraid of anything. Their mother is in a hospital not far away, and the girls miss her.

The house is old, dusty and a little strange. Small black balls of dust run away from the light. And near the house stands a giant tree.

One day Mei follows a small white creature into the forest. She falls through a tunnel of plants and lands on something big, soft and grey. It is Totoro, a huge spirit of the forest. He yawns with an enormous mouth, but Mei is not scared. She falls asleep on his stomach.

The most famous scene happens at a bus stop on a dark, rainy evening. The sisters are waiting for their father. Suddenly Totoro is standing next to them. Satsuki gives him an umbrella. Rain falls on it — drip, drip — and Totoro loves the sound. Then a bus arrives. But it isn't a normal bus. It is a cat.

Hayao Miyazaki made the film at Studio Ghibli in 1988. There are no villains — no bad guys — in it. Only nature, wonder and family. Today Totoro is the symbol of the studio.

title: A Blue Robot Cat
ru: Doraemon — синий кот-робот из будущего с волшебным карманом.
text:
Nobita is a boy of about ten in Tokyo, and his life is a disaster. He gets zero on tests. He is bad at sports. Bigger boys take his toys. And he is always late.

One day a robot comes out of his desk drawer. It is Doraemon, a blue robot cat from the 22nd century. Nobita's great-great-grandson sent him back in time. His job is to help Nobita and make his future better.

Doraemon has a magic pocket on his stomach. From it, he takes amazing gadgets — little machines from the future. The Anywhere Door takes you anywhere: you open it, and you are in Paris. The Bamboo-Copter is a small propeller for your head, and with it you can fly. Of course, Nobita uses them badly, and everything goes wrong.

Doraemon is not perfect either. He loves dorayaki, sweet Japanese pancakes with red bean paste inside. And he is very afraid of mice. Why? A mouse once ate his ears.

Fujiko F. Fujio created Doraemon. The manga started in 1969, and the famous anime series started in 1979. In Asia, Doraemon is as famous as Mickey Mouse. Fans even know his birthday: 3 September 2112. So he is not born yet — but he is already more than fifty years old.

title: A Schoolgirl With a Secret
ru: Обычная школьница Усаги становится героиней Сейлор Мун.
text:
Usagi Tsukino is fourteen, and she is not a hero. She is always late for school. She gets bad marks. She loves cake, video games and sleeping, and she cries a lot.

Then one day she helps a black cat. The cat has a yellow moon on her forehead, and she can talk. Her name is Luna. Luna gives Usagi a magic brooch and tells her the truth: Usagi is Sailor Moon, a warrior who fights evil in the name of the Moon.

Naoko Takeuchi created Sailor Moon. The manga started in 1991, the anime in 1992. The story happens in Tokyo. Soon Usagi finds other girls with powers: Sailor Mercury, Sailor Mars, Sailor Jupiter and Sailor Venus. Each girl has her own planet and her own colour. And a mysterious man in a tuxedo — a black evening suit — helps them and throws red roses.

The transformations are the best part. Usagi lifts her brooch and says the magic words. In a storm of light and ribbons, she becomes Sailor Moon. Then she says her famous words: “In the name of the Moon, I'll punish you!”

The show became a hit in many countries, Russia too. For many girls in the nineties, Usagi was the first hero who was just like them: lazy, funny and brave.

questions.q: Who is Luna?
How old is Usagi?
Where does the story happen?

title: The Boy With a Monkey Tail
ru: Dragon Ball — история Гоку и семи волшебных шаров, которая изменила аниме.
text:
A little boy with a monkey tail lives alone in the mountains. He is very strong, always hungry and completely honest. He has never even seen a girl. Then one day a girl drives along the mountain road in her car and almost hits him.

This is how Dragon Ball begins. Akira Toriyama started the manga in 1984 in the Japanese magazine Weekly Shonen Jump, and the anime by Toei Animation followed in 1986. The boy is Goku, and the girl is Bulma, a clever teenager who loves technology. She is looking for the seven Dragon Balls. If you collect all seven, a huge dragon appears and gives you one wish. Goku has one of the balls at home, a present from his grandpa, so the adventure starts.

Toriyama took the idea from a famous old Chinese story, Journey to the West, about a magic monkey king. Like that monkey, Goku fights with a long stick that can grow, and he flies on a small yellow cloud.

The early Dragon Ball is often very funny. Later it becomes more about fighting. Goku trains with an old master called Master Roshi, meets his best friend Krillin and enters big martial arts tournaments. He learns the Kamehameha, a blue energy beam that he shoots from his hands. Fans all over the world still copy the pose.

Then came Dragon Ball Z, where the fights got even bigger. Many famous manga artists grew up reading Dragon Ball. Toriyama also designed the characters for the Dragon Quest games, so you might know his style even if you don't watch anime.

questions.q: What happens if you collect all seven Dragon Balls?
o: A huge dragon appears and gives you one wish
You can fly on a yellow cloud

questions.q: Where did Toriyama get the idea for Goku?
o: From an old Chinese story about a monkey king

questions.q: What is the Kamehameha?

title: A Young Witch in the City
ru: Юная ведьма Кики уезжает из дома и открывает службу доставки на метле.
text:
In Kiki's world, every young witch must follow an old tradition. When she turns thirteen, she leaves home and lives alone for one year in a new town. So, on a clear night with a full moon, Kiki puts on a dark dress, takes her mother's broom, turns on her little radio and flies away.

Kiki's Delivery Service came out in 1989. Hayao Miyazaki made it at Studio Ghibli, and it was based on a children's novel by Eiko Kadono. It was the biggest Japanese film of the year and one of Ghibli's first big hits.

Kiki isn't alone. Her black cat Jiji travels with her, and he can talk, although he mostly complains. Together they find a big city by the sea, full of old houses, clock towers and boats. It looks like a mix of European cities, and Miyazaki took ideas from Stockholm and the Swedish island town of Visby.

At first the city doesn't seem very friendly. People are busy, and nobody needs a young witch. But a kind baker, Osono, gives Kiki a room above her bakery. Kiki can't do much magic, but she can fly, so she starts a delivery service and carries bags and boxes across the city on her broom. When she loses a toy cat in a forest, poor Jiji has to sit in its place and pretend to be a toy.

There are no evil monsters in this film. The real problems are quiet ones: loneliness, work, money and believing in yourself. Anyone who moves to a new city alone knows exactly how Kiki feels. Maybe that's why adults love this film as much as children do.

questions.q: What must a young witch do when she turns thirteen?
o: Leave home and live alone in a new town for a year

questions.q: Who gives Kiki a room in the city?
What kind of problems are in this film?
o: Quiet ones, like loneliness and believing in yourself

title: A Brother Who Never Gives Up
ru: Танджиро становится охотником на демонов, чтобы спасти сестру.
text:
Tanjiro Kamado is a poor, kind boy who sells charcoal, a black fuel for fires, in the mountains of old Japan. One snowy day he walks down to the village. When he comes back, his family is dead. A demon attacked them in the night. Only his little sister Nezuko is still alive, but she has turned into a demon too.

This is how Demon Slayer begins. Koyoharu Gotouge started the manga in 2016 in Weekly Shonen Jump, and the anime by the studio Ufotable arrived in 2019. The story takes place about a hundred years ago, when Japan already had trains and electric lights, but demons still hunted people in the dark.

Nezuko is not like other demons. She doesn't attack people, and she still protects her brother. She wears a piece of bamboo in her mouth, and in the daytime she sleeps in a wooden box that Tanjiro carries on his back, because sunlight kills demons. Tanjiro wants only one thing: to make her human again. To do that, he must train hard and join the Demon Slayer Corps, a secret army of swordsmen.

On his way he meets two very loud friends. Zenitsu is always scared and crying, but he becomes a great fighter when he falls asleep. Inosuke wears a boar's head, the head of a wild pig, and wants to fight everyone he meets.

The anime looks amazing, especially Tanjiro's water attacks, which look like old Japanese paintings. In 2020 the film Mugen Train became the highest-earning film ever in Japan. It beat even Spirited Away.

questions.q: What does Tanjiro sell?
Why does Nezuko sleep in a box in the daytime?
Which film became the highest-earning film ever in Japan in 2020?

title: A School for Heroes
ru: Мальчик без суперсилы мечтает стать героем и попадает в особую школу.
text:
Imagine a world where most people have a superpower. One person can breathe fire, another can stretch their arms, another has the body of a frog. In My Hero Academia these powers are called Quirks, and about eighty percent of people have one. Being a hero is a real job, with rankings, fans and TV interviews.

Izuku Midoriya wants to be a hero more than anything. He fills notebook after notebook with notes about heroes and their powers. There is just one problem. When he is four, a doctor tells him that he will never have a Quirk. He is completely normal, and in this world that is very unusual.

The story is by Kohei Horikoshi. The manga started in 2014 in Weekly Shonen Jump, and the anime by the studio Bones began in 2016.

Izuku's biggest hero is All Might, the number one hero in Japan, a huge man who smiles all the time and always tells people that everything will be fine. One day Izuku meets him in real life, and everything changes. Soon Izuku is trying to get into U.A. High School, the best school for heroes.

His classmates are a fun group. The most important is Katsuki Bakugo, Izuku's childhood friend and also his bully. Bakugo can make explosions with his hands, and he is angry almost all the time. Ochaco Uraraka can make things float, and serious Tenya Iida runs incredibly fast thanks to engines in his legs.

What makes the series special is Izuku himself. He is not the strongest at the start. He cries a lot, he gets nervous, and he talks to himself. But when someone is in danger, he runs to help before he can even think. And that, the story says, is what a real hero does.

questions.q: What are Quirks?
What did a doctor tell Izuku when he was four?
o: He will never have a Quirk
He will be the strongest hero

questions.q: What can Bakugo do?
o: Run fast with engines in his legs

title: A Castle That Walks
ru: Шляпница Софи, превращённая в старушку, попадает в ходячий замок волшебника Хаула.
text:
Sophie is eighteen, works in her late father's hat shop, and believes she is plain and boring. Then, one evening, a vain and powerful witch walks into the shop and puts a curse on her. When Sophie looks in the mirror, she sees an old woman of about ninety.

So begins Howl's Moving Castle, the 2004 film by Hayao Miyazaki and Studio Ghibli. It is based on a novel by the British writer Diana Wynne Jones, but Miyazaki changed a lot and made the story very much his own.

Instead of crying, Sophie packs a bag and leaves home. In the hills she finds the strangest building in the country: a huge, noisy castle made of towers, pipes and chimneys, which walks across the land on thin metal legs. It belongs to the wizard Howl, who is said to eat the hearts of young girls. Old Sophie walks in anyway, because, as she points out, he will not be interested in her heart now.

Inside, she meets the people who live there. Calcifer is a fire demon who lives in the fireplace and powers the whole castle; he is grumpy, funny and secretly very lonely. Markl is Howl's young apprentice. And Howl himself turns out to be nothing like the rumours: he is handsome, vain and a little cowardly. In one famous scene, Sophie accidentally changes the colour of his hair, and Howl is so upset that green slime starts pouring out of him.

The castle has a magic door with a coloured dial. Turn the dial, open the door, and you are in a different place: a seaside town, a royal city or a field of flowers. This idea is one of the most charming in any Ghibli film.

A strange detail is that Sophie's age keeps changing. When she is brave, angry or in love, she looks younger; when she doubts herself, she grows old again. The film never explains it directly, so you have to watch closely.

Behind the romance and comedy there is a war, and the film shows it as ugly and pointless. The film was nominated for an Oscar, and in the English version Howl is voiced by Christian Bale and Calcifer by Billy Crystal. It is a gentle film about something many people feel: that we are often more beautiful than we believe.

questions.q: What happens to Sophie at the beginning of the story?
o: A witch turns her into an old woman
Howl takes her away to his castle

questions.q: Who powers the castle?
What happens when Sophie feels brave or in love?

title: The Forest Fights Back
ru: Эпический фильм Миядзаки о войне между людьми и духами леса.
text:
Princess Mononoke opens with a nightmare. A giant boar, covered in crawling black worms, crashes out of the forest and attacks a quiet village. The young prince Ashitaka kills it with an arrow, but as it touches him, the darkness passes into his arm. The curse will spread, the village wise woman tells him, and it will eventually kill him. To find out why the boar went mad, Ashitaka rides west, knowing that he can never come back.

Released in 1997, this is one of Hayao Miyazaki's darkest and most ambitious films. It feels less like a fairy tale and more like an epic: there are battles, wounded soldiers, angry gods and real blood.

In the west, Ashitaka finds Iron Town, a busy fortress where people dig iron and make guns. To make iron, they cut down the ancient forest, and the animal gods who live there are fighting back. The leader of Iron Town is Lady Eboshi, a proud and fearless woman. On the other side is San, a human girl raised by a giant white wolf goddess. She hates humans so much that she thinks of herself as a wolf. People call her “Mononoke”, a Japanese word for an angry spirit.

What makes the film special is that there is no simple villain. Eboshi is destroying the forest, but she also gives a home and work to people nobody else wants, including women saved from a hard life and sick people that others are afraid to touch. San is brave and loyal, but she is also full of hatred. Ashitaka refuses to choose a side. He only wants both sides to see each other clearly.

The forest itself is unforgettable. Little white tree spirits called kodama sit in the branches and turn their heads with a soft rattling sound. And at the centre of everything is the Forest Spirit, a mysterious god that looks like a deer by day and becomes something enormous at night.

The film was a huge success in Japan. For a short time in 1997, it was the highest-earning film in Japanese history, until Titanic arrived. Its English script was written by the British author Neil Gaiman.

Princess Mononoke does not give easy answers about people and nature. Perhaps that is why it still feels so modern.

questions.q: Why does Ashitaka travel west?
o: To find out why the boar went mad
To become the leader of Iron Town

questions.q: Who is San?
o: A wise woman from Ashitaka's village
A human girl raised by a wolf goddess

questions.q: Why does the text say there is no simple villain?
o: Even Eboshi does good things for people

title: Two Brothers and a Terrible Mistake
ru: Братья Элрики пытаются вернуть свои тела после неудачного алхимического опыта.
text:
In the world of Fullmetal Alchemist, alchemy is a science with one strict law: Equivalent Exchange. If you want to create something, you must give something of equal value. You can turn stone into a wall or metal into a spear, but you can never get something for nothing.

Two young brothers, Edward and Alphonse Elric, learned this law in the worst possible way. When their mother died, the boys, still children, used everything they knew to bring her back to life. Human transmutation, as it is called, is forbidden, and for good reason. The experiment went terribly wrong. Edward lost his leg. Alphonse lost his whole body. To save his brother, Edward gave up his right arm and attached Alphonse's soul to a huge empty suit of armour.

When the story begins, Edward is fifteen and has metal “automail” limbs made by his childhood friend Winry, a talented and short-tempered mechanic. He has become the youngest State Alchemist in the country, known as the Fullmetal Alchemist. Together, the brothers are searching for the Philosopher's Stone, a legendary object that might let them break the law of Equivalent Exchange and get their bodies back. But the deeper they dig, the darker the secrets they find, and soon they realise that the government they work for is hiding something terrible.

Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood was made by the Japanese studio Bones and shown in 2009 and 2010. It is based on the manga by Hiromu Arakawa. There was already an earlier anime from 2003, but it went in its own direction because the manga was not finished yet. Brotherhood follows the manga to its ending, over 64 episodes.

What makes it so loved is the balance. One minute it is a serious story about war, guilt and the price of mistakes; the next minute Edward is exploding with anger because someone called him short. The characters are full of life, from the flame alchemist Roy Mustang to the gentle giant Alphonse, who cannot eat, sleep or feel anything, but never stops being kind.

For many years, Brotherhood was number one on MyAnimeList, one of the biggest anime rating websites. And here is a fun fact: Hiromu Arakawa grew up on a dairy farm in Hokkaido, and she usually draws herself as a cow.

questions.q: What does the law of Equivalent Exchange say?
o: Alchemy is only allowed for soldiers
To create something, you must give something of equal value
Metal can never be changed into stone

questions.q: What happened to Alphonse after the failed experiment?
o: His soul was attached to a suit of armour

questions.q: How is Brotherhood different from the 2003 anime?
o: It follows the manga to its ending
It has no main characters from the manga
It was made in the United States

title: Your Name: Strangers Who Share a Life
about: Your Name / Kimi no Na wa (2016), Makoto Shinkai
ru: Школьники из Токио и маленького городка просыпаются в телах друг друга.
text:
Imagine waking up in a stranger's body. Not once, but several times a week, without any warning. That is what happens to Mitsuha and Taki, the two teenagers at the heart of Your Name (Kimi no Na wa), Makoto Shinkai's 2016 animated film.

Mitsuha lives in Itomori, a fictional small town in the mountains beside a beautiful lake. She is tired of everything: the quiet, the gossip, the lack of cafés and her family's duties at the local shrine. At one point she shouts out loud that in her next life she wants to be a handsome boy in Tokyo. Taki is more or less exactly that — a high-school student in the capital who rushes between classes and a part-time job at an Italian restaurant.

Then, for no obvious reason, they begin to switch bodies in their sleep. Each wakes up in the other's life, with no memory of what happened the day before. The first part of the film is a sharp and very funny comedy. Mitsuha, in Taki's body, is suddenly far too charming with his female co-worker, while Taki, in Mitsuha's body, keeps forgetting how a girl in a small town is expected to behave. To survive, they start leaving each other notes — in diaries on their phones and even written on their hands. They set rules, break them and send each other angry messages, all without ever meeting.

Meanwhile, a comet is approaching Earth, and the whole country is excited to watch it pass. Saying any more would spoil one of the best twists in modern animation. It is enough to say that the film slowly changes from a comedy into something much bigger, more urgent and more emotional.

Shinkai is famous for his light. His films make everyday places — train platforms, convenience stores, wet streets after rain — look almost unbearably beautiful, and Your Name is full of skies so detailed that you want to pause on every frame. The soundtrack by the Japanese rock band RADWIMPS matters just as much, with songs that seem to push the story forward rather than simply sit behind it.

The film became a huge hit, first in Japan and then around the world, and for several years it was the highest-grossing anime film ever. It also inspired real-life pilgrimages. Fans travel to Tokyo to take photos on a particular staircase near a shrine in the Yotsuya district, where one of the film's most famous scenes takes place.

At its core, Your Name is about a feeling almost everyone knows: the sense that you are searching for someone or something, even if you cannot say what. It is about connection across distance, and about memories that slip away like dreams after waking. Bring tissues — and maybe a pen, just in case you wake up somewhere unexpected.

questions.q: What does Mitsuha wish for early in the film?
o: To move to a quiet town by a lake
To be a handsome boy in Tokyo in her next life
To work at an Italian restaurant

questions.q: How do Mitsuha and Taki communicate with each other?
o: Through notes in phone diaries and on their hands
By calling each other every night
Through a friend who works at the shrine

questions.q: What real place do fans visit because of the film?
o: A staircase near a shrine in Tokyo

title: Cowboy Bebop: Jazz in Outer Space
ru: Культовое аниме о космических охотниках за головами, джазе и одиночестве.
text:
The year is 2071. Humanity has spread across the solar system, travel between planets is easy, and crime has followed people into space. To deal with it, the authorities have brought back an old Wild West tradition: bounty hunters, freelancers who catch criminals for reward money. The ones in Cowboy Bebop are not very good at it.

Created by the Japanese studio Sunrise and directed by Shinichirō Watanabe, Cowboy Bebop first aired in 1998 and ran for just twenty-six episodes. That was enough to make it one of the most influential anime ever made and, for many Western viewers, the first anime they truly fell in love with.

The crew of the spaceship Bebop is a small family of misfits who would never admit to being a family. Spike Spiegel is a lazy, laid-back former gangster with brilliant martial-arts skills and a past he prefers not to discuss. Jet Black, the ship's owner, is a gruff ex-cop with a mechanical arm who grows bonsai trees and cooks meals with almost no meat in them, because the crew is always broke. Faye Valentine is a gambler with a talent for trouble and a mysterious history of her own. Later they are joined by Ed, a hyperactive young computer genius, and Ein, a Welsh corgi who seems to be far smarter than he looks.

What makes the show special is its style. Each episode, called a “session”, mixes genres freely: a noir crime story one week, a comedy the next, then a horror parody or a slow, sad Western. Many episodes work almost like short films, and you can watch them in nearly any order. Underneath, though, runs a darker story about Spike's past, which returns every few episodes and pulls the series toward its unforgettable ending.

Then there is the music. Composer Yoko Kanno and her band, the Seatbelts, created a soundtrack full of jazz, blues, rock and funk, and the explosive opening theme, “Tank!”, is one of the most famous in anime. Music is so central that many episode titles refer to songs or musical styles. Watching Cowboy Bebop feels less like watching a cartoon and more like listening to a great album.

In the United States, the show became a landmark when Cartoon Network's Adult Swim block began broadcasting it in 2001. A feature film followed the same year, and in 2021 Netflix released a live-action version. It was cancelled after a single season, which many fans took as proof that the original is almost impossible to copy.

More than twenty-five years later, Cowboy Bebop still feels fresh. It is cool, funny and stylish, but it is also about loneliness and about people who cannot let go of the past. At the end of most episodes, a short message appears on screen, a casual goodbye to a space cowboy. Fans have been repeating it to each other ever since.

questions.q: Why does Jet often cook meals with almost no meat?
What is unusual about the way the series is structured?
o: Each season follows a different crew
Episodes mix genres freely, and many can be watched in almost any order

questions.q: What happened to Netflix's live-action version?
o: It was cancelled after a single season
It replaced the original on Adult Swim

title: The Last Robot on Earth
ru: Маленький робот-уборщик в одиночку чистит покинутую Землю, пока не встречает EVE.
text:
For the first part of WALL-E, almost nobody speaks. There are no people around, no long explanations, just a small, rusty robot rolling through an empty city full of rubbish. And somehow, it is one of the most touching openings in animated film.

The film, made by Pixar and directed by Andrew Stanton, was released in 2008. It takes place hundreds of years in the future. Humans have filled the Earth with so much waste that they have left it and are waiting in space while robots clean up. Something went wrong, and now only one robot is still working: WALL-E, whose name stands for Waste Allocation Load Lifter: Earth-Class.

Every day, WALL-E collects rubbish, presses it into neat cubes and builds towers taller than skyscrapers. But over the years he has developed a personality. He keeps a collection of interesting objects he finds, like a lighter, a Rubik's Cube and a spork, which confuses him because it is half spoon and half fork. His only friend is a cockroach. In the evenings, he watches an old videotape of a musical and dreams of holding someone's hand.

Then a spaceship lands, and a sleek white robot called EVE appears. She is fast, elegant and has a very powerful gun, which she uses quite a lot. WALL-E falls in love immediately. EVE is on a secret mission, and when she leaves, WALL-E follows her into space, where he discovers what has happened to humanity. On a giant luxury spaceship, people float around in chairs, stare at screens all day and have forgotten how to walk.

Without dialogue, the film depends on sound. WALL-E's voice and many of the film's sound effects were created by Ben Burtt, the sound designer who had given R2-D2 his famous beeps in Star Wars. Listen carefully to the moment when WALL-E's battery is fully charged: you will hear the classic startup sound of an Apple Mac computer.

WALL-E won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature. It is a funny love story, but it also asks a serious question about how we treat our planet and how much we depend on our screens. Luckily, it asks that question very gently, and it never feels like a lecture.

questions.q: Why does WALL-E find the spork confusing?
o: He has never seen a fork before
It is half spoon and half fork
It does not fit in his collection

questions.q: What has happened to the humans on the spaceship?
o: They have forgotten how to walk

questions.q: Who created WALL-E's voice and many of the sound effects?

title: A Voyage Across the Ocean
ru: Дочь вождя с полинезийского острова отправляется в океан, чтобы спасти свой народ.
text:
Moana is the daughter of a chief on the Polynesian island of Motunui, and everyone expects her to lead her people one day. There is just one rule on the island: nobody sails beyond the reef. But the fish are disappearing, the coconuts are going black, and Moana has felt the call of the ocean since she was a toddler. Literally: when she was little, the ocean itself chose her and played with her like a friendly puppy.

Moana was released by Walt Disney Animation Studios in 2016 and directed by Ron Clements and John Musker, the duo behind The Little Mermaid and Aladdin. According to an old legend, the demigod Maui stole the heart of the island goddess Te Fiti, a small green stone with the power to create life, and since then a darkness has been spreading across the islands. Encouraged by her wise and slightly crazy grandmother, Moana sets off to find Maui and make him return the heart.

Maui is voiced by Dwayne Johnson, and he is a wonderful mix of hero and show-off. He is huge, his tattoos move and comment on his actions, and he can change into animals with his magic fishhook. Unfortunately, he lost the hook a long time ago, and he is not exactly keen to help a teenage girl who does not even know how to sail properly.

The film is full of colour and comedy. Moana's companion on the voyage is Heihei, a rooster so stupid that he tries to eat stones. There is a gang of coconut pirates and a giant crab who loves shiny treasure. But the heart of the film is the theme of wayfinding: the traditional Polynesian art of navigating across the open ocean by reading the stars, the waves and the wind. The filmmakers worked with experts from Pacific islands to show this culture with respect.

The music was written by Lin-Manuel Miranda, the creator of Hamilton, together with Opetaia Foa'i and Mark Mancina, and the song “How Far I'll Go” was nominated for an Oscar. Moana was voiced by Auliʻi Cravalho, a teenager from Hawaii who was chosen after a long search.

Here is a surprise: in several European countries, the film is called Vaiana, not Moana, mainly because the name Moana was already registered as a brand there. A sequel, Moana 2, followed in 2024.

questions.q: What is the one rule on Moana's island?
o: Nobody may talk to the ocean

questions.q: What can Maui do with his magic fishhook?
What is wayfinding?
o: Navigating by the stars, waves and wind

title: Superheroes With Normal Problems
ru: Семья супергероев, которым запретили спасать мир, пытается жить обычной жизнью.
text:
What happens to superheroes when the world decides it doesn't want them anymore? In The Incredibles, they get boring office jobs.

Bob Parr was once Mr. Incredible, the strongest and most popular hero in the city. Then people the heroes had saved began to sue them for damage and injuries, and the government decided to ban superhero work completely. Fifteen years later, Bob sits in a tiny office at an insurance company, squeezed behind a desk that is far too small for him, and listens to his boss lecturing him about profits. He misses the old days so much that he secretly goes out at night with his best friend, Frozone, to listen to police radio and save people.

At home, things are not easy either. His wife Helen, once the stretchy hero Elastigirl, wants a normal, quiet life for the family. Their daughter Violet is a shy teenager who can turn invisible and create force fields, which is very convenient when you want to hide from the boy you like. Their son Dash runs faster than anyone, but he is not allowed to do sports, because he would win too obviously. And baby Jack-Jack seems to have no powers at all.

When a mysterious organisation offers Bob a secret mission, he cannot resist. Soon the whole family has to put on their masks again, and they discover that being a team is harder than being heroes.

The film was written and directed by Brad Bird and released by Pixar in 2004. It was Pixar's first film where all the main characters are human, which was a real technical challenge: skin, hair and clothes are very difficult to animate. The style looks like a spy film from the 1960s, with jazz music, secret islands and stylish villains.

One of the most popular characters is Edna Mode, a tiny, very serious fashion designer who makes costumes for superheroes and absolutely hates capes. She was voiced by Brad Bird himself.

The Incredibles won two Oscars, including Best Animated Feature. Fans had to wait fourteen years for Incredibles 2, which came out in 2018 and begins at exactly the same moment where the first film ends.

questions.q: Why were superheroes banned?
o: They became too old to work
People sued them for damage and injuries

questions.q: Why is Dash not allowed to do sports?
Who voiced Edna Mode?

title: The Monsters in Your Closet
ru: Монстры Салли и Майк работают на фабрике детских криков, пока в их мир не попадает девочка.
text:
When you were a child, were you afraid of the monster in your closet? According to Pixar, you were right. It was there. But it was just doing its job.

Monsters, Inc., directed by Pete Docter and released in 2001, takes place in Monstropolis, a city of monsters powered by an unusual source of energy: children's screams. At the Monsters, Inc. factory, thousands of closet doors connect the monster world with children's bedrooms all over the human world. Professional “scarers” walk through the doors at night, frighten the children, and collect their screams in yellow tanks.

The best scarer in the company is James P. Sullivan, called Sulley, a huge blue-and-purple monster with horns and thick fur. His best friend and assistant is Mike Wazowski, a small green ball with one enormous eye, a lot of jokes and even more confidence. Sulley is voiced by John Goodman and Mike by Billy Crystal, and their friendship is the heart of the film.

There is one big problem in Monstropolis: monsters are terrified of children. They believe that a single touch from a human child could be deadly. So when a little girl accidentally follows Sulley through a door into the monster world, the whole city panics. Sulley names her Boo, and he and Mike have to hide her, return her home and avoid their jealous rival Randall, a purple lizard-like monster who can change colour and disappear against any background.

Boo is one of the funniest characters in the film, even though she hardly says a real word. She was voiced by Mary Gibbs, the young daughter of a Pixar artist. She was too little to sit still and read lines in a recording studio, so the team followed her around with a microphone and recorded whatever she said while she played.

Technically, the hardest part of the film was Sulley's fur. Each of his many hairs had to move separately when he walked or when the wind blew, and this was a huge challenge for computers at the time.

The film's song “If I Didn't Have You”, by Randy Newman, won an Oscar. And here is a fun fact: Billy Crystal once said no to voicing Buzz Lightyear in Toy Story and later regretted it, so he was very happy to say yes to Mike.

title: Soul: What Are We Actually Here For?
ru: Джазовый пианист оказывается в мире душ и вынужден задуматься о смысле жизни.
text:
Most children's films are about kids learning to grow up. Soul, Pixar's 2020 film, is about a middle-aged man discovering that he may have been living the wrong way. It is also, somehow, very funny.

Joe Gardner, voiced by Jamie Foxx, is a middle-school music teacher in New York who dreams of being a professional jazz pianist. His students are not exactly gifted, his mother wants him to accept a safe, permanent teaching job, and his big break never seems to come. Then, one day, it does: he gets the chance to play with the famous saxophonist Dorothea Williams, voiced by Angela Bassett. Joe is so happy that he walks around the city without looking where he is going — and falls straight into an open manhole.

Suddenly he is a small blue soul on a moving walkway heading toward a huge white light, the Great Beyond. Joe has no intention of dying on the best day of his life, so he runs. He escapes into the Great Before, a soft, pastel world where new souls get their personalities before they are born on Earth. There he is mistaken for a mentor and paired with 22, voiced by Tina Fey, a cynical soul who has spent centuries refusing to go to Earth because she thinks life is not worth the trouble. Famous figures from history have tried to inspire her and failed. Joe sees an opportunity: if he helps 22, maybe he can get back to his body in time for the show.

The film's look is a brilliant contrast. New York is drawn in rich, realistic detail — steam, crowded subways, the warm lights of a barbershop and a jazz club. The Great Before is gentle and abstract, run by counselors who are all called Jerry and look like a single moving line drawn by Picasso. The music follows the same idea. Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross wrote the strange electronic sounds of the soul world, while jazz musician Jon Batiste composed and played Joe's piano pieces. Their work won the Academy Award for Best Original Score, and Soul also won Best Animated Feature.

Joe was Pixar's first Black lead character, and the filmmakers worked closely with musicians and cultural advisers to make his world feel real, from the conversations in the barbershop to the way his hands move on the keys. Because of the COVID-19 pandemic, the film went straight to Disney+ instead of cinemas, so many people discovered it at home, in a year when life had suddenly become very small.

That timing gave its message extra force. Soul asks what a “spark” really is. Is it a great passion, a career, a purpose? Or could it be something smaller — a slice of pizza, a seed falling from a tree, the wind on a subway platform? The film's answer is gentle but surprisingly brave for a family movie: you do not need a grand purpose to deserve your life. You just need to live it.

title: The Iron Giant: The Flop That Became a Classic
ru: Как провалившийся в прокате мультфильм о мальчике и гигантском роботе стал классикой.
text:
In 1999, Warner Bros. released an animated film about a lonely boy and a fifty-foot robot that fell from the sky. Hardly anyone went to see it. Today The Iron Giant regularly appears on lists of the best animated films ever made, and its director has become one of the most respected names in animation. How did a flop turn into a classic?

The story is set in 1957, in the small coastal town of Rockwell, Maine. The Soviet Union has just launched Sputnik, the first artificial satellite, and Americans are nervous about anything in the sky. One night, nine-year-old Hogarth Hughes goes into the woods and finds a giant metal robot tangled in power lines. Hogarth saves it, and the two become friends.

The Giant has no memory of where it came from. It is curious, gentle and enormously hungry — not for food, but for metal. Hogarth hides it at a scrapyard owned by Dean, a relaxed beatnik artist who turns junk into sculptures and soon has a much bigger problem than unsold art. Meanwhile, a government agent named Kent Mansley arrives in town, convinced that something dangerous is hiding nearby and determined to become a hero by finding it.

The film is loosely based on The Iron Man, a 1968 children's book by the English poet Ted Hughes, and it was the first feature film directed by Brad Bird, who had previously worked on The Simpsons. It asks a serious question for a family movie: if you were built to be a weapon, are you doomed to become one? Hogarth's answer, more or less, is that you are who you choose to be.

So why did it fail? Mostly because almost nobody knew it existed. The studio's marketing was weak and late, and the film reached cinemas without much advertising, toys or attention. Families went to see other films, and The Iron Giant quietly disappeared from theaters.

But the people who did see it never forgot it. Critics praised it highly, and when it came out on video and began appearing on television, a new audience discovered it at home. Its reputation grew year after year. By 2018 the Giant was popular enough to appear as a hero in Steven Spielberg's Ready Player One, a long way from box-office failure.

Brad Bird, meanwhile, moved to Pixar, where he directed The Incredibles and Ratatouille, both of which won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. Many of the qualities fans love in those films — sharp humor, real emotion and action that actually matters to the characters — were already there in The Iron Giant.

What makes the film last is its sincerity. It is funny and exciting, with a thrilling final act, but above all it is about friendship, fear and the choice to be good. Watch it once, and you may understand why its fans still get emotional at the mere mention of Superman.
